title: Per-note context searches for Q3 and cote-120 observations
scope: All 36 items in the frozen Q3 research draft; each listed query was executed over every line of every file supplied under context/. No supplied scan image was opened.
method: Case-insensitive Python regular-expression search on the original UTF-8 file lines, without normalization. Results preserve complete matched lines, original 1-based line numbers, the current scanpage marker for transcriptions, and the enclosing Markdown headings for notes and registers. Every searched file receives an entry even with zero hits. Multiple queries matching one line are deduplicated at line level, with every matching query ID retained.
interpretation_limit: These are lexical search results, not newly verified mathematical conclusions. Context research notes remain first-pass leads; register statuses remain the returns' claims under their recorded review limits. The relation adds/restates/differs/contradicts and the mathematical comparison are stated in the corresponding frozen note. A missing term does not establish absence from an original manuscript.

matches.text: **Status:** “unproved claim” means that the asserted step is not demonstrated in the cited manuscript passage, not that it is false or unknown. Proposed constructions and examples labeled “own idea” carry a confidence assessment and a reason, and no novelty claim is made. Published results are used only within their stated hypotheses: comparisons of coverings, fundamental groupoids, constructible sheaves, topoi, and full homotopy types are kept distinct. The bibliography supplies APA references and exact supporting theorem or section locations.

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

It adds a covering-extension claim to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 136–137, where the starred locus and its local embedding are described but this equivalence is not proved. The task is to show both extension and full faithfulness for coverings across the omitted deeper loci in the germ, with the topology and puncturing fixed; merely noting that the base inclusion is dense does not justify either property.

matches.text: The repeated demand for generization and a “structure d'extension” has a concrete application to the earlier programme of recovering the moduli groupoids and their graph operations. These pages add geometric machinery to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 104, which asks to determine $\Pi_1M_{g,I}$, the extensions $S\Pi_1M_G$, and the maps induced by graph generization, and to scans 78–89, where those extensions are already organized around boundary germs. A useful comparison would track a single node-smoothing meridian through the normal torsor, the punctured germ, and the graph-generization map, checking its orientation, kernel, and permutation action before asserting that the abstract gluing construction realizes the full earlier programme.

This **restates** the source/target orientation of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 113, and **adds** the closure condition that an incoming smaller branch remains in $\Sigma$ whenever its target branch is selected. matches.text: The admission that the reduction “ne s’explicite pas aisément, au niveau des groupoïdes fondamentaux” concerns information lost when passing from a closed immersion of topoi to its induced groupoid map. It **restates** the distinction between the mixed recollement topos and its multigaloisian reflection in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and **adds** the concrete problem of recovering open complements from that reduced data. A simple illustration is that both pairs $(\mathbb C,\{0\})$ and $(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ induce, up to equivalence, the same arrow of trivial connected fundamental groupoids, while their open complements have respectively fundamental group $\mathbb Z$ and no objects. This illustration concerns the bare groupoid arrow, and scan 180 supplies a separate warning about higher cohomology lost by a proposed constructible reconstruction; neither warning identifies the comparison in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 167, with the one refuted on 180.

matches.text: The “quatre pièces” are the global open stratum $\mathbb C^*$, the point $P$, the disk germ $\mathbb D$, and its punctured germ $\mathbb D^*$, with the list completed on scan 164. This **restates** the difference between a germ and its residual germ in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and **adds** their placement beside global pieces in the flag construction. In particular, $V_0=V_0^*=\mathbb C^*$ does not already include the recovered ambient $\mathbb C$, and a disk germ has not been identified with its center as a topos merely because their ordinary fundamental groupoids are equivalent. The word “germe,” inserted in place of “disque,” keeps the neighborhood-filter information that the construction requires.

matches.text: The relative “pièces de construction” suggest testing a description by exit-path data that retains directed specialization and its homotopies, rather than using only the separate fundamental groupoids of the pieces. This proposal **adds** a possible organization of the flag tubes to the noninvertible recollement transformation of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, while respecting that file’s distinction, on scan 166, between the mixed topos and its galoisian reflection. Treumann’s exit-path classifications supply comparison targets under conical-stratification and tameness hypotheses; identifying these germ flags with exit paths remains a separate task (Treumann, 2009, Theorems 1.2 and 7.14). Confidence is medium because the needed specialization data are present in the program; constructing the comparison and checking the stratification hypotheses remain necessary, and scan 180 rules out concluding that a constructible category of sets alone recovers the ambient homotopy type.

matches.text: The list distinguishes “point” from “germe de disque,” although their ordinary homotopy types agree after choosing a disc representative. This **restates**, in a particularly small model, the distinction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, between the closed-stratum topos $B_S$, the mixed neighborhood topos $B_{D;S}$, and their different canonical maps. A replacement of the disc by the point is therefore justified only after specifying which invariant is being retained and what happens to the punctured-disc attachment. The four-object diagram should be tested at the level of its maps and gluing functors, since an equivalence of individual homotopy types alone does not supply the asserted reconstruction.

It **restates** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where points of $D_d$ include a chosen codimension-$d$ germ and the map to $X$ is a local immersion. Replacing this object by the set-theoretic union of its images would discard data subsequently needed for finite étale flag covers and branch monodromy. A useful verification of later formulas is therefore to distinguish equality of image strata from equality of the branch-parametrizing spaces themselves.

matches.text: The observation that the “nouveaux” elementary topoi first occur in (281) identifies a specific role for $\mathbb D\times\mathbb D^*$ and $\mathbb D^*\times\mathbb D$. It **adds** partially punctured neighborhood pieces to the intersection/flag combinatorics in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 113. The full nine-object product of the two three-object gluing spans records these mixed overlaps as well as $\mathbb D^*\times\mathbb D^*$, whereas the diagram for the complement of the origin omits the final bidisc piece. Thus a proposed minimal system of building blocks must justify any omission of a mixed piece by an explicit reconstruction, not merely by agreement of the separate strata.

In particular, the rank-zero endpoint at index $0$ and the displayed definition of the top term cannot both be read as the standard relative normal bundle without an additional convention or a notational revision. matches.text: The emphatic “est une équivalence d’homotopie” concerns the projection of the affine torsor onto the punctured quotient bundle. It **adds** a topological conclusion to the affine-translation distinction in `LM_140-3_text.tex`, scans 294 and 299. For an actual locally trivial affine bundle over a paracompact analytic-manifold base, a partition of unity combines local affine sections into a continuous section, and affine interpolation contracts each fiber toward it, giving a direct proof without requiring a holomorphic splitting. The remaining obligation is to identify the manuscript objects with such bundles before transporting this argument to a germ or topos model.

A proof would need a topological tubular model preserving the relevant partial boundary deletions, followed by a comparison with the chosen topos or germ construction. The existence of a normal bundle by itself establishes neither a holomorphic linearization nor a canonical homeomorphism, and neither stronger conclusion should be read into (292).

177-03 — The empty-flag and open-stratum margin

matches.text: The system with its “morphismes canoniques” is expected to “reconstituer” the groupoids, the quasi-Galois topoi, and “par là aussi” the homotopy types, including $X$. This **adds** a full homotopy-reconstruction claim to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–168, which distinguish the mixed glued topos from its fundamental-groupoid reflection and separately question their acyclicity comparisons. The sphere on scan 180 has aspherical open and closed strata as well as a circular punctured neighbourhood, so asphericity of the individual pieces cannot justify the stated passage through the ordinary glued topos. A proof must specify the gluing operation and the comparison to the original topos, including whatever coherent or higher information survives it.

179-01 — Aspherical pieces do not by themselves prove the reconstruction

matches.text: “Ce qui est le cas dans la situation de Teichmüller!” invokes asphericity for every required $D^*_{d_*}$. This **restates** the $K(\pi,1)$ input for $M_G$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 80, and the contractible Teichmüller universal cover asserted in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 188 and 257–258, but **adds** its application to the particular flag strata used here. The verification must identify the product and finite-cover descriptions of those strata, and specify whether the object is a modular topos, an orbifold or stack, a rigidified cover, or a coarse quotient; the cited context itself keeps group actions and mixed groupoids explicit in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 76–78. At a codimension-one zero or pole, its residue is the integer $v(h)$, so the failed nonvanishing condition leaves a calculable ramification contribution rather than a well-defined nonzero tangent vector (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Confidence is high for this local statement because it is the same Kummer valuation computation as RN094-01; a global extension across singular strata is not asserted.

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: The invitation “Le cas du genre $0$” has an explicit editorial test: $U=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q((t))}\setminus\{0,t,1,\infty\}$ has all four punctures rational and $H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbf Z_\ell)\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell(1)^3$, so its $t$-adic inertia acts trivially for every $\ell$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). This adds the family deferred by “Je vais pas le faire ici” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 62, to the cross-ratio description on scan 61. The cross-ratio $t$ meets the boundary, and blowing up the collision of $0$ and $t$ produces two rational components with two marked points and a node on each, so the pointed curve has bad reduction although its compactification is smooth. Confidence is high because the boundary collision and Kummer homology are explicit; only the local $t$-adic inertia is trivial on $H_1$, while the full arithmetic action still contains the cyclotomic character.

The arithmetic statement is valid for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated $X/K$ with connected geometric fibre: $1\to\pi_1(X_{\bar K})\to\pi_1(X)\to G_K\to 1$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.14.3, Tag 0BTX). It does not justify the stronger assertion for every simply connected $T$, and unrestricted field extension of a nonproper scheme in characteristic $p$ already supplies a counterexample, detailed in 110-O1 (Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). Confidence: high in the arithmetic theorem and in the distinction between it and the unrestricted reading of (12).

matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

This **differs** in scope from **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19 and 25**, where the ambient curve is already projective and smooth. Nagata compactification supplies a proper compactification for a separated finite-type $U/K$, but gives no regularity conclusion; a singular $U$ cannot be an open subscheme of a regular $X$, and even for regular $U$ a regular compactification is an additional existence input (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Theorem 38.33.8, Tag 0F41). The fixed fields of decomposition and inertia are respectively the fraction fields of the henselization and strict henselization, so fixing the prolongation $x'$ gives the asserted embedded subgroups, whereas forgetting it leaves conjugacy classes (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.13.1, Tag 0BSW). This **adds** a quotient presentation to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 26–28**, where the local inertia maps are attached to an already specified curve and boundary. For regular integral finite-type $U/K$, every centered valuation's inertia dies on finite étale covers, while the codimension-one inertia already generates the kernel by finite normalization and regular-target purity (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BTD and 0BMB). matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

The example and consequence in **130-O1–130-O2** give a valuation ring of $\mathbf Q(x,y)$ with value group $\mathbf Z$ and residue field $\mathbf Q$, hence a noetherian DVR at a point of manuscript codimension two, contradicting this assertion. This **differs** from the divisorial curve-local “jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**: being a DVR is a valuation-theoretic property, whereas being divisorial imposes the additional residue-transcendence condition (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.18, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high because the explicit value group and residue field determine both sides of the contradiction; the counterexample is cross-referenced rather than proved twice.

This **adds** a relative birational space over a general base to the local curve-trait construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**. For an integral base one may use its proper birational modifications and valuations of its function field with centers on it; Temkin's relative construction goes further, using separated morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, without an excellence requirement, and its general stalk description uses semivaluation rings rather than necessarily valuation rings of one field (Temkin, 2011, Sections 1.1 and 2.1–2.2). Confidence: high in this precise modern continuation, with the modification category and integral versus general relative setting made explicit rather than inferred from the short margin.

At the compatible center on this model, one of the two standard charts of $\mathbf P^1$ makes $h$ or $h^{-1}$ regular, which proves the valuation property without using resolution of singularities. This supplies a completion of the manuscript argument and adds an inverse-system construction to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; compare Temkin (2011, Lemma 2.2.2) and the element-or-inverse criterion in The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., Tag 00I8, Lemma 10.50.5). matches.text: The question « quelle est sa signification topologique? » suggests replacing the bare incidence complex by a diagram carrying the fundamental groupoids of strata, the local lattices of branches, and the normal torus torsors, before taking any homotopy colimit. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123 and 128–133, already supplies the lattices, torsors, flags, and the distinction between the undecorated and decorated groupoids; cote 149 adds the arithmetic maps into the fundamental group of the complement. For fine saturated log schemes locally of finite type over $\mathbf C$, Carchedi et al. (2017, introduction and Theorem 6.4) compare the Kato–Nakayama space and the infinite root stack after profinite completion, including torus fibers whose ranks follow the strata. **Our confidence: medium**, because these fibers match the manuscript’s local ingredients, whereas identifying its particular formal or étale object $U_\infty$ with the appropriate boundary of that construction still requires a comparison theorem and cannot follow from the incidence complex alone.

Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

matches.text: | BISITE D.6 | Proper base change is a coefficient theorem. Consider a cartesian square of locally compact Hausdorff spaces \[ \begin{array}{ccc} X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\[-2pt] {\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\[-2pt] Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y. \end{array} \] If $f$ is proper, the canonical mate $g^*f_*\to f'_*g'^*$ is an equivalence on sheaves of spaces. It is also an equivalence on sheaves with values in a stable bicomplete infinity-category. These are ordinary infinity-sheaves; hypercompletion is not silently substituted. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HTT 7.3.1.18; Volpe). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.8 | The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. This does not identify $f_!$ with the left adjoint $f_\sharp$ of D.7. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HA 5.5.5.1; Volpe 6.9). |

matches.text: The parenthetical “défini à iso unique près ?...” asks for a uniqueness statement about the neighborhood germ, and the sentence about descent to multiplicities is still exploratory. This adds an immersion-relative construction to the germ around an actual subset defined by its neighborhood filter in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and to the filter-based category of germs on scan 242. A proof needs a stated category of germs over $Y$ and an account of local branch separation: uniqueness over the ambient object is a different assertion from uniqueness of a bare germ or of a chosen tubular parametrization.

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

matches.text: The phrase “de noyau un quotient de $T_{d_0,\ldots,d_r}$” is consistent with the exact sequence $\pi_2(B)\to\pi_1((\mathbb C^*)^r)\to\pi_1(P)\to\pi_1(B)\to1$ for a locally trivial torus bundle over a connected base. It qualifies the extension description in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 130–131, where the margin already warns that the full lattice kernel requires a condition on $\pi_2$. The connecting homomorphism can kill meridians, so a proof should identify its image and the induced local-system action rather than assert an injection of the entire lattice; the fibration exact sequence is the relevant classical result (Serre, 1949–1950, §1).

This **adds** a selection of whole normalized branches to the branch-intersection construction in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 108, rather than simply pulling back a closed subset. For two transverse branches with $\Sigma$ equal to one branch, the full inverse image in $D_1$ also contains the intersection point on the other normalized branch, whereas the revised definition selects only the component lying wholly in $\Sigma$. matches.text: The claim that the “donnée … est équivalente” to compatible subsets of $\pi_0(D_d)$ makes the admissible closed $\Sigma$ recoverable from the global component data rather than arbitrary local labels. This **adds** a closed-subset classification to the branch-labeling torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 109 and 117, where permutation monodromy is already built into the flag spaces. To prove both directions one must show that the component selections respect the incidence maps and descend to a locally finite union of branch intersections, and that every such union yields exactly those selections. Working with $\pi_0(D_d)$ incorporates the global branch identifications; independently labeling local branches without their transport could produce a selection that does not descend.

matches.text: The second version asserts that the semisimplicial family of germ topoi has colimit “équivalente canoniquement” to $V^*_{\Sigma,X}$, but gives no descent proof. It **adds** a general admissible-support gluing statement to the nonformal neighborhood structure anticipated in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 133, and must be distinguished from the two different gluing constructions in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166. A proof should define the comparison pseudodiagram and establish effective descent for its local branch charts, including the relevant comparison $2$-cells. Lurie’s Theorem 6.1.3.9 and Proposition 6.1.3.10 give a possible modern descent test for diagrams inside an infinity-topos, but do not identify this colimit of varying germ topoi without an additional construction (Lurie, 2009, pp. 548–549 in the updated author PDF).

matches.text: The phrase “c’est donc un crible” suggests checking admissible supports and all selected flags by finite incidence calculations in a branch chart, then imposing invariance under branch transport. This proposal **adds** a computational use to the Boolean branch poset and its permutation torsor in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106, 109, and 116: choose local intersections, close the selection under incoming arrows, and retain precisely the flags whose final vertex is selected. Confidence is high for the finite local calculation because the branch poset and the closure rule are explicit; confidence in a global implementation is conditional on correctly retaining monodromy and the analytic component data. This is a suggested consistency check and construction procedure, not a claim of novelty or a proof of the topos gluing theorem.

matches.text: The assertion expressing “$\Pi_1(X)$ … comme somme amalgamée” is the curve case of gluing the complement to genuine neighborhoods of the missing points. It **restates** the cospan and hole-filling construction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 162 and 168, with the closed-point groupoids now discrete. For an actual open tubular-neighborhood cover, Brown’s Theorem 3.4 proves the fundamental-groupoid pushout using an object set meeting every component of the overlap, so disconnected punctured neighborhoods cause no problem (Brown, 1967, pp. 391–392). Passage from those actual neighborhoods to the manuscript’s germ topoi still requires the relevant fundamental-groupoid comparison; the theorem does not assert an equivalence of topoi.

matches.text: The identity for the “trace de $\Sigma_1$” asserts that restricting the neighborhood germ of $\Sigma'$ in $\Sigma''$ to $\Sigma_1$ gives the germ of $\Sigma'\cap\Sigma_1$ in $\Sigma_1$, without requiring $\Sigma'\subset\Sigma_1$. This **adds** a closed-admissible-subset base-change statement to the neighborhood-filter definition in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, whose residual germs also show why an arbitrary trace cannot be identified from its center alone. At the ordinary neighborhood-filter level, closedness of $\Sigma_1\subset\Sigma''$ proves the required cofinality: extend an open neighborhood $U_1\subset\Sigma_1$ to an ambient open $W$, then use $W\cup(\Sigma''\setminus\Sigma_1)$ as a neighborhood of $\Sigma'$. This argument does not apply to an arbitrary nonclosed trace such as a punctured complement, and an analytic-topos version must retain the intended closed-immersion interpretation.

matches.text: The admission that the reduction “ne s’explicite pas aisément, au niveau des groupoïdes fondamentaux” concerns information lost when passing from a closed immersion of topoi to its induced groupoid map. It **restates** the distinction between the mixed recollement topos and its multigaloisian reflection in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and **adds** the concrete problem of recovering open complements from that reduced data. A simple illustration is that both pairs $(\mathbb C,\{0\})$ and $(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ induce, up to equivalence, the same arrow of trivial connected fundamental groupoids, while their open complements have respectively fundamental group $\mathbb Z$ and no objects. This illustration concerns the bare groupoid arrow, and scan 180 supplies a separate warning about higher cohomology lost by a proposed constructible reconstruction; neither warning identifies the comparison in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 167, with the one refuted on 180.

matches.text: The assertion that the global line “se reconstitue” as $\mathbb C^*\amalg_{\mathbb D^*}\mathbb D$ requires a precise category, because $\mathbb D$ is introduced as a germ rather than a specified open disc. It **adds** an explicit analytic local/global model to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 162–166, where the diagram of punctured neighborhoods, open part, and closed part produces both a glued topos and a distinct fundamental-groupoid topos. For a chosen open disc, the two sets $\mathbb C^*$ and $\mathbb D$ cover $\mathbb C$, so ordinary sheaf descent supplies a concrete test case; a germ formulation still needs independence under shrinking and the corresponding universal property. Passing directly from that cover to an asserted pushout of unspecified “types” would skip the principal definition that the formula leaves open.

matches.text: The formula $D_d=\coprod_{|J|=d}D_J$ uses a disjoint union, so it retains separate branch sheets even when their images meet in $X$. It **restates** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where points of $D_d$ include a chosen codimension-$d$ germ and the map to $X$ is a local immersion. Replacing this object by the set-theoretic union of its images would discard data subsequently needed for finite étale flag covers and branch monodromy. A useful verification of later formulas is therefore to distinguish equality of image strata from equality of the branch-parametrizing spaces themselves.

matches.text: A useful test is to require that the “diagramme … de type produit” produce equivalent gluings in either coordinate order and that the comparison commute with all four elementary face squares. This proposal **adds** a neighborhood-level coherence check to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 114 and 118, where associativity and a commuting flag-composition square are explicit pieces of the deployment structure. It would isolate a finite obstruction before attempting the general statement, but it must be formulated in the chosen category of topoi or homotopy types, since preservation of colimits by products is not part of the manuscript’s definitions. **Confidence: high** as a necessary consistency test, because a single proposed product diagram cannot yield incompatible results from its two parenthesizations; no sufficiency theorem is claimed.

matches.text: The “filtration canonique” labels $\check N_{d_*,d_i}$ with rank $d_i$, but (283) identifies it with a bundle for the immersion $D_{d_*}\to D_{d_i}$. This **differs** from `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 120 and 135–136, where the immersion into the codimension-$d_i$ stratum has codimension $d_0-d_i$. In particular, the rank-zero endpoint at index $0$ and the displayed definition of the top term cannot both be read as the standard relative normal bundle without an additional convention or a notational revision. The notes should preserve the conflict and test the two possible index conventions separately, rather than selecting one because it makes later formulas work.

matches.text: The phrase “immersion locale” matters because the flag spaces need not be globally embedded subspaces of their targets. This **restates** the local-immersion and finite-étale factorization in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 108, 128, and 136, but **adds** bundles and exact-sequence identifications on those flags. After settling the notation, a proof can construct the usual regular-immersion bundles in branch charts and then verify that their canonical transition maps descend through the finite étale flag covers; the scheme-theoretic local algebra is recorded in Stacks Project Authors (2026c, Lemma 31.22.6). The missing part is compatibility of that descent with every flag-forgetting morphism, not merely local exactness in one coordinate chart.

matches.text: “Si $X$ est compact” is used to obtain finitely many intrinsic strata, “qui sont loc. compactes,” with the warning that finiteness need not survive restriction to an open set. This **adds** a global finiteness conclusion to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where finiteness concerns branch sets at individual points, not the number of global strata. A proof can try a finite cover by charts with finitely many local pieces, but must justify that each local connected piece belongs to one globally constructed stratum; local compactness additionally requires the relevant separation convention and locally closed chart models. These are separate checks, and neither follows simply from finiteness of the local incidence posets.

matches.text: Use the drawing with “$7$” incident strata as a concrete test of the germ nerve: the planar model has a central minimum, three ray strata, and three sectors, giving seven objects, nineteen weakly ordered pairs, and thirty-seven weakly ordered triples at the centre. This **adds** a non-Boolean test to the finite powerset models in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106, 116, and 128, while preserving an explicit check of the composable-pair description on scan 188. In the corresponding finite global-chart model, the source spaces are copies of each source closure indexed by its incident chains, so finite étaleness of those projections can hold even though the poset is not Boolean; the example thus separates two properties mentioned together on scan 189. Confidence is high in the finite count and medium in transferring that global-chart topology to every local representative, and no conclusion about reconstruction of an arbitrary stratified space is drawn.

heading_path: Research notes: MPL 147, scans 138–190

188-04 — A comparison problem with profinite exodromy

matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

This **restates** the strict inverse-image relation in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 129, and **generalizes** its finite flag-cover description in scans 128 and 132, which uses the finite branch set and first-vertex-preserving maps. A proof must separate finiteness of a fibre from local constancy of the family, and identify how the frontier and connected-germ conditions give a stable incidence set as the origin moves along an intrinsic stratum. matches.text: The three-ray drawing has seven incident strata “en comptant $\bullet$ lui-$=$,” so its local order cannot be the full powerset of a finite set. This **differs** from the normal-crossing hypothesis in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 116, and **adds** an explicit witness that the general local-stratification framework has non-Boolean incidence. The count is interpreted in the planar model as the centre, three rays, and three sectors; it does not by itself disprove the Segal identity, finite étaleness, or any particular homotopy-reconstruction assertion. A useful axiomatization should therefore keep the Boolean local-order condition separate from the categorical and topological conditions.

matches.text: The local order is said to be “isomorphe … à l'ens des parties d'un ens. fini,” whereas `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 106, explicitly makes the germ-intersection order antiisomorphic to $\mathcal P(I(x))$, and scan 108 writes the opposite-order notation. Thus the present statement **differs in its stated order convention**, although it need not contradict the earlier claim, since taking complements identifies a finite Boolean lattice with its opposite. The question is which identification is intended for source, target, and face maps, where reversal matters even though the abstract ordered-set isomorphism type and cardinality test do not. The transcription is unchanged and no arrow is reversed to force a convention.

This **adds** a way to audit the separation already made in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 132–133, between formal flag-cover relations and nonformal generisation, and prevents the success of the former from being treated as a proof of the latter. These 157 notes accompany the complete diplomatic transcription of scans 91–136 of Montpellier cote 149. They were prepared after all 46 page transcriptions were finished and the context-opening gate was recorded; the combined transcription and every page file remain identical to their frozen versions. Quotations and source anchors refer to those frozen readings, including their unresolved symbols and canceled passages, while locations identify approximate manuscript rows, paragraphs, displays, or margins rather than LaTeX line numbers.
heading_path: MPL_149_091–136 — Research notes

matches.text: The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. Recovering a rational section from an arbitrary compatible family of abstract group splittings is a stronger existence problem and does not follow from closed-point density.

This differs from the local organization in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 75 (“faire un raisonnement local général”), which first fixes the trait and its fraction field before adjoining roots. The mathematical comparison suggests $G_{\operatorname{Frac}(A^{sh})}$ for inertia and $G_{\operatorname{Frac}(A^h)}$ for decomposition, but it cannot decide which decoration the author intended to write (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). Identifying the resulting extension with the special fiber also uses the good smooth-pair specialization hypotheses, as in SGA 1, Exposé XIII, §§2.8–2.10 (Grothendieck, 1971/2003). The parenthetical converse identifying this group condition with the domain of definition is consequently a claim about the given geometric section and its boundary behavior, not a formal consequence for every abstract section.

matches.text: The assertion that “$D=S\setminus S^{\prime}$ est purement de codim $1$” follows if the rational map extends to the compactification and the pulled-back boundary equation remains a non-zero-divisor. In that situation the inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor, hence has pure codimension one; the local pullback condition is essential (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01WQ). This adds a global divisor interpretation to the “indice de ramification” discussed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 45. The parenthesis about $g\geq1$ or a one-dimensional base should therefore be kept as part of the author’s extension argument, rather than treating purity as a property of every indeterminacy locus on an arbitrary higher-dimensional base.

matches.text: The observation that the closed-point fields are “extensions finies de ce $k$” permits $G_{k(s)}$ to be identified with an open subgroup of $G_k$, after compatible embeddings of separable closures have been chosen. This restates the warning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, that the residue algebraic closure is not canonically the previously chosen closure of the ground field. Taking the complete regular curve model organizes its places intrinsically, but does not remove the conjugacy choice of a lift $s^{\prime}$ or supply a preferred splitting of $D_{s^{\prime}}\to G_{k(s)}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). Consequently the current formulas should be compared as compatible based constructions or as conjugacy classes, according to which choices have been fixed.

This restates the peripheral compatibility in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 84, and connects the degeneration to the tangent-parametrized family on scan 79. The decomposition-group normalizer description supports the cuspidal interpretation (Tamagawa, 1997, Remark 7.5). The cusp can be determined up to conjugacy while the actual lift continues to depend on the tangent or Kummer splitting, so the passage does not select a unique actual action.

matches.text: The acknowledgment that “bonne réduction” had been implicit needs the pointed-pair meaning: a proper smooth compactification together with a relatively étale boundary. This restates the finite étale marking condition in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 5, and agrees with Tamagawa’s Definition 5.1 (1997). Smoothness of the compactification alone allows punctures to collide, and even a smooth nonproper model can lose punctures in its special fiber. The genus-zero case proposed in the scan 103 margin therefore tests a real missing boundary condition, as made explicit in RN103-01.

matches.text: The conjecture “ssi il y a bonne réduction” has a precise later theorem for hyperbolic pointed curves over a discrete valuation field. Tamagawa proves that good reduction of the pair is equivalent to trivial outer inertia on one, equivalently every, prime-to-residue-characteristic pro-$\ell$ geometric fundamental group (Tamagawa, 1997, Theorem 5.3). This adds a group criterion to the marked-curve setting of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 5, with its “fini étale” boundary. In the manuscript’s residue-characteristic-zero situation, this validates the nonabelian a)–b) comparison, without validating the proposed substitutions of $H_1$ in c) and d).

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

In `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 403, an arithmetization is additional structure on a potential curve, accompanied by admissible-lift data, and scan 405 separately asks how to recover that structure. The present margin differs by asserting existence of some arithmetization while the main text asks whether a particular action obtained from a chosen splitting is geometric. Those quantifiers are distinct, so the marginal assertion does not resolve the main admissibility question, whatever the uncertain adjective ultimately means.

matches.text: The phrase “structure à l’infini” connects the action problem to the marked dual graph of a stable degeneration. This restates the “maquette” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 11, and adds an arithmetic question to the three boundary partitions of the four-pointed line on scan 61. Independent node-smoothing parameters give local boundary directions, while the graph distinguishes a separating node from a loop contributing to the Jacobian’s toric part (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5 and Lemma 1.17). Consequently the graph supplies useful test cases for the conjectural equivalences without itself determining the entire arithmetic outer action.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: The allowance of “une extension finie de $k$” restricts the residual action to an open subgroup of $G_k$. This restates the open-subgroup issue in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 412, whose reverse direction is explicitly queried by “et inversement ?”. Such a restriction should not be identified with a ramified extension of the local generic field that kills its inertia: decomposition and residue quotients distinguish those operations (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). For instance, the twist in RN103-03 becomes constant after adjoining $\sqrt t$, whereas its residual action is already geometric over $\mathbf Q$ before making any residue extension.

These contextual ideas supply candidate constraints, but do not identify “pas trop loufoque” with any one of them. The quadratic-twist example supplies geometric actual actions at bad reduction, so any definition intended to include all geometric actions would also prevent f)$\Rightarrow$a) as stated; it does not assign a meaning to the author’s undefined phrase.

matches.text: The invitation “Le cas du genre $0$” has an explicit editorial test: $U=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q((t))}\setminus\{0,t,1,\infty\}$ has all four punctures rational and $H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbf Z_\ell)\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell(1)^3$, so its $t$-adic inertia acts trivially for every $\ell$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). This adds the family deferred by “Je vais pas le faire ici” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 62, to the cross-ratio description on scan 61. The cross-ratio $t$ meets the boundary, and blowing up the collision of $0$ and $t$ produces two rational components with two marked points and a node on each, so the pointed curve has bad reduction although its compactification is smooth. Confidence is high because the boundary collision and Kummer homology are explicit; only the local $t$-adic inertia is trivial on $H_1$, while the full arithmetic action still contains the cyclotomic character.

matches.text: The question “comment voir que e) implique bonne réduction” has a counterexample in its stated generality: over $K=\mathbf Q((t))$, let $E_t:y^2=x^3-t^2x$ and $U_t=E_t\setminus\{O\}$, the ramified quadratic twist of $U_0$ for $E_0:y^2=x^3-x$. The isomorphism $(X,Y)\mapsto(tX,t^{3/2}Y)$ over $K(\sqrt t)$ has descent cocycle $[-1]$, so inertia acts as $-1$ on $H_1$ and rules out good reduction, whereas the uniformizer-based residue splitting fixing $\sqrt t$ pulls the full outer action back to that of $U_0/\mathbf Q$ (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). The current passage adds a reduction implication to the realization meaning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410; this example disproves that addition using the local splitting construction of scan 75. matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

matches.text: The question « quelle est sa signification topologique? » suggests replacing the bare incidence complex by a diagram carrying the fundamental groupoids of strata, the local lattices of branches, and the normal torus torsors, before taking any homotopy colimit. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123 and 128–133, already supplies the lattices, torsors, flags, and the distinction between the undecorated and decorated groupoids; cote 149 adds the arithmetic maps into the fundamental group of the complement. For fine saturated log schemes locally of finite type over $\mathbf C$, Carchedi et al. (2017, introduction and Theorem 6.4) compare the Kato–Nakayama space and the infinite root stack after profinite completion, including torus fibers whose ranks follow the strata. **Our confidence: medium**, because these fibers match the manuscript’s local ingredients, whereas identifying its particular formal or étale object $U_\infty$ with the appropriate boundary of that construction still requires a comparison theorem and cannot follow from the incidence complex alone.

matches.text: The phrase « l'action extérieure “cyclotomique” » invites a comparison between the system of maps $T^J\to\pi_{U/K}$ and the stabilizers of all roots of the boundary divisors: in characteristic zero, their geometric fibers involve $\varprojlim_n\mu_n^J$, with the arithmetic cyclotomic action and, when branches are not globally labeled, their permutation action. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, describes the corresponding integral local systems and torus torsors, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, identifies the one-branch inertia with a Tate module in its discussion of tangential splittings. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3 and Theorem 6.22) identify the relevant Kummer étale topos with that of the infinite root stack, providing a candidate precise setting for this comparison. **Our confidence: medium**, since the local stabilizers and actions agree in the characteristic-zero normal-crossing case, but this alone neither proves that their maps into a global fundamental group are injective nor recognizes all valuations from that group.

Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

The cross-ratio $t$ meets the boundary, and blowing up the collision of $0$ and $t$ produces two rational components with two marked points and a node on each, so the pointed curve has bad reduction although its compactification is smooth. Confidence is high because the boundary collision and Kummer homology are explicit; only the local $t$-adic inertia is trivial on $H_1$, while the full arithmetic action still contains the cyclotomic character.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

matches.text: The margin’s “n'est pas étale” concerns integral separation of boundary points, a property stronger than their rationality over the generic field. This differs from `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 150, where the generalized-Jacobian description begins with a boundary already “étale de degré $3$”. The proposed genus-zero investigation therefore isolates precisely why a boundary permutation representation, even together with the compactification’s homology, need not recover good reduction of the pointed curve.

This **adds** a larger separably closed field of a base point to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 22**, which describes a separable residue-field closure, and scan 108 of the present manuscript itself explicitly says “clôtures séparables dans $\Omega$”. Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

matches.text: For each $h\in L^\times$, take the closure of the graph of the rational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbf P^1_K$ defined by $h$, and normalize it, obtaining another proper normal model of $L/K$. At the compatible center on this model, one of the two standard charts of $\mathbf P^1$ makes $h$ or $h^{-1}$ regular, which proves the valuation property without using resolution of singularities. This supplies a completion of the manuscript argument and adds an inverse-system construction to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; compare Temkin (2011, Lemma 2.2.2) and the element-or-inverse criterion in The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., Tag 00I8, Lemma 10.50.5). Confidence: high for the unrestricted proper normal-model category, because the graph construction is proper birational and the two-chart alternative is exhaustive; a restricted indexing category requires a separate cofinality check.

matches.text: Compactify two models $U_1,U_2$ to $X_1,X_2$, choose a common proper normal birational refinement $Z$, and put $W=p_1^{-1}(U_1)\cup p_2^{-1}(U_2)$. By the valuative criterion of properness, a valuation has center in $W$ exactly when it has center in one of the $U_i$, so $W$ represents the union; in characteristic zero a further resolution gives the same conclusion for unrestricted regular models. This contradicts the literal negative NB under those model conventions and adds a finite-union test to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; Temkin (2011, Theorem 3.5.1(i)) independently supports the relevant closure property. matches.text: Take $X=\operatorname{Bl}_p\mathbf P^2_{\mathbf Q}$, let $D\simeq\mathbf P^1$ be the exceptional divisor, and consider complex points: its normal bundle is $\mathcal O(-1)$, and $U=X\setminus D\simeq\mathbf P^2\setminus\{p\}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 02OS). The punctured tube retracts to the Hopf bundle $S^1\to S^3\to S^2$, whose connecting map $\pi_2(S^2)\to\pi_1(S^1)$ is an isomorphism, so the fiber fundamental group is not injected into that tube (Hatcher, 2002, Examples 4.45 and 4.51). The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. matches.text: The deletion of “séparé” in favour of “un faisceau,” together with the margin read uncertainly as “est connue quand on la connaît localement,” suggests that uniqueness from local data is being distinguished from existence of a global representative. Its internal nerve then realizes as $S^2$ with an interval attached at that point, which deformation retracts to $S^2$, whereas the discrete two-object incidence category realizes as an interval. matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

matches.text: The conclusion “de deuxième espèce” should be compared with the later restriction to splittings arising from a uniformizer, rather than silently identifying those two families. This differs in scope from `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 79, which explicitly distinguishes the whole Kummer-cohomology torsor from a smaller “sous-famille” called geometric and parametrized by a $k^\times$-torsor. Our elementary test over $\mathbf Q$ is a compatible family of classes of $p^{a_n}$, with $(a_n)\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ not arising from an ordinary integer: its valuation at $p$ prevents it from being the Kummer class of any rational number (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

matches.text: The last line of scan 119, manuscript page 59, proposes $I_{x'}=\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I_{x'})$. This **differs** from the curve-loop situation in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 117 and 190** once a divisorial residue field has positive transcendence degree over $K$, and the explicit example in 119-O1 disproves the unrestricted formulation. Combining 119-O2 with intersection of normalizers gives the appropriate general expression $\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I)=D\cap\pi_{L/K}$, whose quotient by $I$ can contain the geometric residue Galois group; **LM_140-3_text.tex, scan 418** also warns that a related algebraic-group self-normalizer analogy fails while its proposed profinite analogue still requires checking. Confidence: high in the counterexample and the intersection formula, with the latter context serving as a warning about categories rather than as a proof.

matches.text: To test $I_{x'}=\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I_{x'})$ at the bottom of scan 119, take $K=\mathbf Q$, $L=\mathbf Q(x,y)$, and the $x$-adic divisorial valuation, whose residue field is $\mathbf Q(y)$. Inside $\pi_{L/K}=G_{\overline{\mathbf Q}(x,y)}$, its decomposition group $D_{\mathrm{geom}}$ contains $I\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)$ normally and satisfies $D_{\mathrm{geom}}/I\simeq G_{\overline{\mathbf Q}(y)}\ne1$, the nontriviality being witnessed by adjoining $\sqrt y$, so $D_{\mathrm{geom}}\subset\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I)$ already strictly contains $I$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BTX and 0BUA). This **differs** from the curve-peripheral normalizer sequence in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 190**, because the present residue retains a geometric direction, explicitly allowed by scan 118's transcendence-degree $n-1$ parenthesis. Confidence: high in this explicit counterexample; it refutes the second presumed equality in transcendence degree two and does not refute the first equality proved in 119-O2.

matches.text: For the hyperbolic curve $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q}\setminus\{0,\sqrt2,-\sqrt2\}$, the degree-two boundary divisor is connected over $\mathbf Q$ but splits into two geometric cusps exchanged by $G_{\mathbf Q}$. A selected geometric inertia conjugacy class is stabilized by $G_{\mathbf Q(\sqrt2)}$, whereas the pair is $G_{\mathbf Q}$-equivariant; distinct cusp classes are not identified by geometric conjugation (Stix, 2012, Proposition 16). This adds a concrete scope test and agrees with the rational-boundary restriction and finite-base-change discussion in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 83–84. Confidence: high for the Galois and inertia calculation, because the two points and their stabilizer are explicit, while the intended component convention on 136 remains a reading question.

matches.text: The phrase « l'action extérieure “cyclotomique” » invites a comparison between the system of maps $T^J\to\pi_{U/K}$ and the stabilizers of all roots of the boundary divisors: in characteristic zero, their geometric fibers involve $\varprojlim_n\mu_n^J$, with the arithmetic cyclotomic action and, when branches are not globally labeled, their permutation action. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, describes the corresponding integral local systems and torus torsors, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, identifies the one-branch inertia with a Tate module in its discussion of tangential splittings. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3 and Theorem 6.22) identify the relevant Kummer étale topos with that of the infinite root stack, providing a candidate precise setting for this comparison. **Our confidence: medium**, since the local stabilizers and actions agree in the characteristic-zero normal-crossing case, but this alone neither proves that their maps into a global fundamental group are injective nor recognizes all valuations from that group.

matches.text: The reference to $\mathfrak m_{s_\alpha}/\mathfrak m_{s_\alpha}^{2}$ and the « faisceau conormal » suggests tracing a chosen first-order parameter through the normal-torus construction used for higher-codimension boundary strata. **Context comparison — adds a link:** `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 73–75, treats Kummer torsors of tangential splittings, whereas `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, constructs punctured **normal** line bundles and their product torsors; the conormal line on scan 95 is their dual in the Cartier-divisor situation. A useful check is to compute the effect of $t\mapsto ut$ on the associated splitting class and to track the duality when comparing Chern classes, rather than identifying the two torsor conventions by notation alone (Talpo & Vistoli, 2018, §3, supplies a modern divisor-root framework). **Our confidence: medium**, because the first-order and line-bundle data are visibly present in both manuscripts, but a full identification must specify the parameter, basepoint, and duality conventions.

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al.
