matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

The fixed fields of decomposition and inertia are respectively the fraction fields of the henselization and strict henselization, so fixing the prolongation $x'$ gives the asserted embedded subgroups, whereas forgetting it leaves conjugacy classes (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.13.1, Tag 0BSW). At the compatible center on this model, one of the two standard charts of $\mathbf P^1$ makes $h$ or $h^{-1}$ regular, which proves the valuation property without using resolution of singularities. This supplies a completion of the manuscript argument and adds an inverse-system construction to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; compare Temkin (2011, Lemma 2.2.2) and the element-or-inverse criterion in The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., Tag 00I8, Lemma 10.50.5). This adds a failure of injectivity for valuation images on one model to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 117–118, and differs from separating distinct curve cusps because both valuations have the same boundary center. matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

This adds local section data to the branch bookkeeping in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 107, rather than assuming that a single rank-one inertia group captures every branch. If a boundary parameter pulls back as $u\prod_{j=1}^{r}t_j^{m_j}$, Kummer theory sends the $j$th tame inertia generator to $m_j$ times the target generator, while the unit supplies the residual Kummer class (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). matches.text: The question “comment voir que e) implique bonne réduction” has a counterexample in its stated generality: over $K=\mathbf Q((t))$, let $E_t:y^2=x^3-t^2x$ and $U_t=E_t\setminus\{O\}$, the ramified quadratic twist of $U_0$ for $E_0:y^2=x^3-x$. The isomorphism $(X,Y)\mapsto(tX,t^{3/2}Y)$ over $K(\sqrt t)$ has descent cocycle $[-1]$, so inertia acts as $-1$ on $H_1$ and rules out good reduction, whereas the uniformizer-based residue splitting fixing $\sqrt t$ pulls the full outer action back to that of $U_0/\mathbf Q$ (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). The current passage adds a reduction implication to the realization meaning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410; this example disproves that addition using the local splitting construction of scan 75. Confidence is high because the coordinate change and descent cocycle are explicit; this is an editorial counterexample with finite nontrivial inertia, and no extra semistability assumption is being inserted into the manuscript.

This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

This **adds** a universal relative assertion to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 188**, whose specific curve-moduli fibration explicitly retains a preceding $\pi_2$-term before obtaining a short exact sequence. matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

matches.text: For “A t-on une réciproque ?” on scan 120, take $K=\mathbf C$, $L=\mathbf C(t)$, $U=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf C}$, and the valuation at infinity on $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf C}$. Its nontrivial inertia maps trivially to $\pi_1(U)=1$, since the complex affine line is simply connected and the étale group is its profinite completion, but the unique center of the valuation on the proper model is $\infty\notin U$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Section 64.27, “Comparison,” Tag 03VD, and Lemma 58.13.5, Tag 0BUA). This **differs** from the restricted curve classes in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 20**, and is permitted by scan 115's explicit allowance for algebraically closed $K$. Confidence: high because both the trivial target group and the missing center are explicit; the example does not disprove the additional marginal restriction, and the same test can be transferred to $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Q}$ using characteristic-zero base-change invariance and the arithmetic sequence (Landesman, 2024, Theorem 1.1; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BTX).

matches.text: The NB beside (31) on scan 121, manuscript page 60, says “Cette définition ne dépend pas de l'hypothèse de résolution des sing” because normal proper models may replace regular ones. This agrees with the modern Riemann–Zariski construction as a locally ringed inverse limit over proper birational models; normal models suffice, and regular models give the same limit when a resolution theorem supplies a cofinal family of them (Temkin, 2011, Introduction and Proposition 2.2.1). It **differs** from **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, whose projective system of group schemes is representable as a scheme because its transition maps are affine, a condition not supplied for the proper birational transitions here. Confidence: high in the resolution-independent normal-model construction and in the conditional cofinality statement; no unrestricted resolution theorem is being assumed.

matches.text: At the end of scan 121, manuscript page 60, “ce n'est pas un schéma !” is qualified by the insertion “si $n\geq2$”, and scan 122 adds that $n=0,1$ are the only scheme cases. For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). Confidence: high under this normal finite-type model interpretation; neither the mere existence of nonnoetherian stalks nor the incorrect noetherian-stalk assertion assessed in 122-CJ1 would prove nonschematicity.

matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

With the manuscript's codimension $n-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(V)$, lift $n-1$ algebraically independent residue elements to $V$ and choose a normal proper model where those lifts are regular at its center: the center has codimension one, its local ring is a DVR dominated by $V$, and hence equals $V$, giving an essentially finite-type divisorial valuation ring. This **adds** the higher-dimensional residue criterion to the curve-local “anneau-jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, and agrees with the description of Zariski prime divisors by codimension-one local rings and residue transcendence degree in Pop (2006, pp. 294–295). Confidence: high in the divisorial characterization, including the converse supplied by a prime divisor on a normal model; it neither identifies all discrete valuations with divisorial ones nor resolves the abbreviated handwritten adjective.

matches.text: The question « quelle est sa signification topologique? » suggests replacing the bare incidence complex by a diagram carrying the fundamental groupoids of strata, the local lattices of branches, and the normal torus torsors, before taking any homotopy colimit. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123 and 128–133, already supplies the lattices, torsors, flags, and the distinction between the undecorated and decorated groupoids; cote 149 adds the arithmetic maps into the fundamental group of the complement. For fine saturated log schemes locally of finite type over $\mathbf C$, Carchedi et al. (2017, introduction and Theorem 6.4) compare the Kato–Nakayama space and the infinite root stack after profinite completion, including torus fibers whose ranks follow the strata. **Our confidence: medium**, because these fibers match the manuscript’s local ingredients, whereas identifying its particular formal or étale object $U_\infty$ with the appropriate boundary of that construction still requires a comparison theorem and cannot follow from the incidence complex alone.

matches.text: The phrase « l'action extérieure “cyclotomique” » invites a comparison between the system of maps $T^J\to\pi_{U/K}$ and the stabilizers of all roots of the boundary divisors: in characteristic zero, their geometric fibers involve $\varprojlim_n\mu_n^J$, with the arithmetic cyclotomic action and, when branches are not globally labeled, their permutation action. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, describes the corresponding integral local systems and torus torsors, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, identifies the one-branch inertia with a Tate module in its discussion of tangential splittings. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3 and Theorem 6.22) identify the relevant Kummer étale topos with that of the infinite root stack, providing a candidate precise setting for this comparison. **Our confidence: medium**, since the local stabilizers and actions agree in the characteristic-zero normal-crossing case, but this alone neither proves that their maps into a global fundamental group are injective nor recognizes all valuations from that group.

matches.text: The claim that $\hat X\setminus D$ « a un caractère invariant » should be tested by comparing the pairs or boundary maps associated with different compactifications, keeping the boundary object separate from the homotopy type of the whole complement. **Context comparison — differs in scope:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 127–133, builds a system on open strata and their normal torsors, not merely a single invariant of the open variety; cote 149’s formulation should retain that additional relative information. Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

matches.text: The reference to $\mathfrak m_{s_\alpha}/\mathfrak m_{s_\alpha}^{2}$ and the « faisceau conormal » suggests tracing a chosen first-order parameter through the normal-torus construction used for higher-codimension boundary strata. **Context comparison — adds a link:** `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 73–75, treats Kummer torsors of tangential splittings, whereas `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, constructs punctured **normal** line bundles and their product torsors; the conormal line on scan 95 is their dual in the Cartier-divisor situation. A useful check is to compute the effect of $t\mapsto ut$ on the associated splitting class and to track the duality when comparing Chern classes, rather than identifying the two torsor conventions by notation alone (Talpo & Vistoli, 2018, §3, supplies a modern divisor-root framework). **Our confidence: medium**, because the first-order and line-bundle data are visibly present in both manuscripts, but a full identification must specify the parameter, basepoint, and duality conventions.

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

It **adds** a broader reconstruction objective to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 166–168, which already distinguishes the mixed topos from its fundamental-groupoid replacement and treats acyclicity as a further question. matches.text: The “quotient canonique” in (286) divides $\check N_{d_*,d''_0}$ by $\check N_{d_*,d'_0}$ under $d''_0\le d'_0$, whereas (282) writes the larger-index terms as larger subbundles. This **differs** from the consistent rank-decreasing coordinate projection in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 124–125, and the fiber dimension $d'_0-d''_0$ stated later on current scan 177 points toward the opposite rank convention. The issue is independent of whether one calls the bundles normal or conormal: a quotient requires a specified subbundle, and the displayed inclusion order does not supply it as written. No correction is proposed for the frozen source; a later mathematical reconstruction must make its revised convention explicit.

matches.text: The emphatic “est une équivalence d’homotopie” concerns the projection of the affine torsor onto the punctured quotient bundle. It **adds** a topological conclusion to the affine-translation distinction in `LM_140-3_text.tex`, scans 294 and 299. For an actual locally trivial affine bundle over a paracompact analytic-manifold base, a partition of unity combines local affine sections into a continuous section, and affine interpolation contracts each fiber toward it, giving a direct proof without requiring a holomorphic splitting. The remaining obligation is to identify the manuscript objects with such bundles before transporting this argument to a germ or topos model.

This **adds** a global finiteness conclusion to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where finiteness concerns branch sets at individual points, not the number of global strata. This adds a comparison between the local groupoid in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, and the conjugacy classification of splittings on scan 63 (“mod. autom. intérieurs”). For a fixed based extension, a splitting gives an actual conjugation action on its geometric kernel, whereas changing the base point or transport path changes the comparison by an inner automorphism. The latter dependence is explicit in SGA 1, Exposé XIII, §2.10, and explains why the author’s insistence on “effectives” requires compatible choices (Grothendieck, 1971/2003).

Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. After fixing one section $s$, another has the form $s^{\prime}(g)=c(g)s(g)$ with $c$ a continuous nonabelian $1$-cocycle in $\pi$, and its action is $\operatorname{Int}(c(g))\alpha_s(g)$. Thus changing the section of (31) preserves the outer action but can change the actual action and its point-theoretic interpretation; this is a direct calculation from multiplication in the extension.

The geometric hyperbolic group is center-free, so $\pi\simeq\operatorname{Inn}(\pi)$ identifies an inner-valued action of $T$ with a continuous homomorphism $T\to\pi$ (Tamagawa, 1997, Proposition 1.11). This restates the distinction between splittings and kernel conjugacy in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63: the outer restriction is independent of the selected lift. It does not assert that the resulting homomorphism $T\to\pi$ is zero, and an existential “one splitting” should not be replaced by a vacuous universal statement when no splitting is available.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

matches.text: At scan 122, the opening continuation of scan 121 says that codimension-one points “correspondent exactement” to the indicated finite-type “jauges”, with “ess.” versus “ext.” still marked as a reading doubt. With the manuscript's codimension $n-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(V)$, lift $n-1$ algebraically independent residue elements to $V$ and choose a normal proper model where those lifts are regular at its center: the center has codimension one, its local ring is a DVR dominated by $V$, and hence equals $V$, giving an essentially finite-type divisorial valuation ring. This **adds** the higher-dimensional residue criterion to the curve-local “anneau-jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, and agrees with the description of Zariski prime divisors by codimension-one local rings and residue transcendence degree in Pop (2006, pp. 294–295). Confidence: high in the divisorial characterization, including the converse supplied by a prime divisor on a normal model; it neither identifies all discrete valuations with divisorial ones nor resolves the abbreviated handwritten adjective.

matches.text: | BISITE D.6 | Proper base change is a coefficient theorem. matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |

This adds a stronger comparison to the normal-torsor definitions on `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–127, and to the locally immersed flag geometry on scans 135–137. A proof must handle those deeper intersections and demonstrate an equivalence of the appropriate covering categories, not just compute a meridian group at a single smooth boundary point; scan 147's marginal reduction to $D'^{*}$ is itself a further assertion needing justification.

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

matches.text: The phrase “de noyau un quotient de $T_{d_0,\ldots,d_r}$” is consistent with the exact sequence $\pi_2(B)\to\pi_1((\mathbb C^*)^r)\to\pi_1(P)\to\pi_1(B)\to1$ for a locally trivial torus bundle over a connected base. It qualifies the extension description in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 130–131, where the margin already warns that the full lattice kernel requires a condition on $\pi_2$. The connecting homomorphism can kill meridians, so a proof should identify its image and the induced local-system action rather than assert an injection of the entire lattice; the fibration exact sequence is the relevant classical result (Serre, 1949–1950, §1).

matches.text: The “Th de recollement” claims an equivalence of topoi between the colimit of the flag-indexed punctured germs and $X^{*\infty}$. It adds a descent theorem to the half-simplicial groupoid programme in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131–135, and is stronger than the fundamental-group calculations associated with gluing in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–169. A proof must specify the categorical colimit, establish effective descent for sheaves along the augmented flag system, and explain how the local normal-crossing models cover the boundary germ; a comparison of $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ alone proves less than the stated theorem.

matches.text: The claim “contre exemple encore plus simple: les feuilletages!” needs its scope specified, since ordinary foliations of positive transverse dimension have infinitely many local plaques and are not locally finite partitions as in 181 a). The search for local equivalence relations and foliations in the supplied primary files found no matching earlier construction; the nearest germ construction, `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, instead uses a finite local branch set, so the present passage **adds** a broader analogy whose hypotheses are not supplied there. matches.text: “Si $X$ est compact” is used to obtain finitely many intrinsic strata, “qui sont loc. compactes,” with the warning that finiteness need not survive restriction to an open set. This **adds** a global finiteness conclusion to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where finiteness concerns branch sets at individual points, not the number of global strata. A proof can try a finite cover by charts with finitely many local pieces, but must justify that each local connected piece belongs to one globally constructed stratum; local compactness additionally requires the relevant separation convention and locally closed chart models. These are separate checks, and neither follows simply from finiteness of the local incidence posets.

Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

This adds the family deferred by “Je vais pas le faire ici” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 62, to the cross-ratio description on scan 61. The cross-ratio $t$ meets the boundary, and blowing up the collision of $0$ and $t$ produces two rational components with two marked points and a node on each, so the pointed curve has bad reduction although its compactification is smooth. Confidence is high because the boundary collision and Kummer homology are explicit; only the local $t$-adic inertia is trivial on $H_1$, while the full arithmetic action still contains the cyclotomic character.

This differs from `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 150, where the generalized-Jacobian description begins with a boundary already “étale de degré $3$”. In RN103-01, all punctures are rational and their boundary permutation module is constant, yet their closures collide; the abelianized representation consequently loses the cross-ratio degeneration. The proposed genus-zero investigation therefore isolates precisely why a boundary permutation representation, even together with the compactification’s homology, need not recover good reduction of the pointed curve.

matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

This **adds** a relative birational space over a general base to the local curve-trait construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**. For an integral base one may use its proper birational modifications and valuations of its function field with centers on it; Temkin's relative construction goes further, using separated morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, without an excellence requirement, and its general stalk description uses semivaluation rings rather than necessarily valuation rings of one field (Temkin, 2011, Sections 1.1 and 2.1–2.2). matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |

matches.text: The transvection example can be checked directly if the uncertain upper-right matrix entry is the retained first reading $1$: the generator acts by $(x,y)\mapsto(x+y,y)$ and fixes the line $y=0$. An equivariant linear section of the quotient would send $1$ to a vector $(a,1)$ fixed by the generator, but that vector is sent to $(a+1,1)$, so the tangent extension does not split and an equivariant tubular diffeomorphism inducing the prescribed normal identification cannot exist. This adds an explicit verification to the proposed descent in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 259–260, where local coordinates have no such equivariance constraint; confidence is high conditional on the entry $1$, and the calculation is a test of the author's example rather than a claim of novelty.

matches.text: A useful test of “un quotient de $T$” and “par l’image des $\pi_2$” is the zero-section divisor in the total space of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$: its punctured normal bundle identifies with $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$ by sending a nonzero vector in its tautological line to that vector. This total space retracts to $S^3$, so its fundamental group is zero, whereas the trivial punctured line bundle over $\mathbb P^1$ has fundamental group $\mathbb Z$; the contrast is the Hopf-bundle instance of the connecting map discussed by Serre (1949–1950, §§1, 5). This **adds** an explicit example to the normal-line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, and the $\pi_2$ caveat on scan 130, and tests the models on current scans 175–178 as well as the earlier qualification on scan 148. Confidence is high in the calculation because the identification is explicit, and medium in its usefulness for the full diagram comparison because one piece does not settle canonical transition maps; no claim is made that this particular bundle occurs in the moduli application.

For a fixed based extension, a splitting gives an actual conjugation action on its geometric kernel, whereas changing the base point or transport path changes the comparison by an inner automorphism. The latter dependence is explicit in SGA 1, Exposé XIII, §2.10, and explains why the author’s insistence on “effectives” requires compatible choices (Grothendieck, 1971/2003).

This restates the warning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, that the residue algebraic closure is not canonically the previously chosen closure of the ground field. matches.text: The question “qu’attendre d’une telle action ?” can first be separated into its formal and geometric parts. It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. After fixing one section $s$, another has the form $s^{\prime}(g)=c(g)s(g)$ with $c$ a continuous nonabelian $1$-cocycle in $\pi$, and its action is $\operatorname{Int}(c(g))\alpha_s(g)$. Thus changing the section of (31) preserves the outer action but can change the actual action and its point-theoretic interpretation; this is a direct calculation from multiplication in the extension.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

matches.text: For “Ladite extension est admissible” on scan 102, the counterexample to e)$\Rightarrow$a) survives the stronger quantifier “for every splitting”: for any section $s:G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the restricted descent cocycle is the continuous quadratic character $\chi_t\circ s$. Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. Confidence is high because the argument restricts the actual geometric descent cocycle before applying fundamental groups, rather than inferring full geometricity from $H_1$.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

matches.text: At scan 106, display (4) and its following sentence, “la clôture alg. de $k(x)$ dans $\Omega$” accompanies a canonical comparison whose first subscript remains $\alpha$ or $X$. This **adds** a larger separably closed field of a base point to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 22**, which describes a separable residue-field closure, and scan 108 of the present manuscript itself explicitly says “clôtures séparables dans $\Omega$”. Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. Confidence: high in this distinction, medium in the intended terminology, and low in the marked subscript; it does not assert invariance of $\pi_1(X_\Omega)$ under changing the base field of $X$.

The arithmetic statement is valid for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated $X/K$ with connected geometric fibre: $1\to\pi_1(X_{\bar K})\to\pi_1(X)\to G_K\to 1$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.14.3, Tag 0BTX). It does not justify the stronger assertion for every simply connected $T$, and unrestricted field extension of a nonproper scheme in characteristic $p$ already supplies a counterexample, detailed in 110-O1 (Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). Confidence: high in the arithmetic theorem and in the distinction between it and the unrestricted reading of (12).

This **adds** a relative component factor to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 83**, where a finite base extension separates geometric connected components and makes the relevant images over the base Galois group explicit. A precise finite case is the Stein factorization of a proper flat finitely presented map with geometrically reduced fibres, for which $Y'\to Y$ is finite étale (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.15.1, Tag 0BUN); the closed image of $\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y)$ instead determines a pointed profinite cover in Galois theory, without automatically being an open subgroup or a finite cover. This **restates** the extension perspective of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 71**, and **adds** an explicit warning to that file's conjugation calculations in scans 48–50. matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

The fixed fields of decomposition and inertia are respectively the fraction fields of the henselization and strict henselization, so fixing the prolongation $x'$ gives the asserted embedded subgroups, whereas forgetting it leaves conjugacy classes (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.13.1, Tag 0BSW). matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

Combining 119-O2 with intersection of normalizers gives the appropriate general expression $\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I)=D\cap\pi_{L/K}$, whose quotient by $I$ can contain the geometric residue Galois group; **LM_140-3_text.tex, scan 418** also warns that a related algebraic-group self-normalizer analogy fails while its proposed profinite analogue still requires checking. For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The assertion adds a geometric mechanism to the expressly “non-formel” missing first-face map in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 133–135, where only the maps preserving the first flag element had been constructed. A proof must produce the functor on covering categories, show that it is independent of the tubular choices, and verify its compatibility with the already defined face and degeneracy maps; the curve construction of Deligne (1989, §§15.3–15.7) provides a precise comparison case, not a proof of the full flag statement.

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

matches.text: The identity for the “trace de $\Sigma_1$” asserts that restricting the neighborhood germ of $\Sigma'$ in $\Sigma''$ to $\Sigma_1$ gives the germ of $\Sigma'\cap\Sigma_1$ in $\Sigma_1$, without requiring $\Sigma'\subset\Sigma_1$. This **adds** a closed-admissible-subset base-change statement to the neighborhood-filter definition in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, whose residual germs also show why an arbitrary trace cannot be identified from its center alone. At the ordinary neighborhood-filter level, closedness of $\Sigma_1\subset\Sigma''$ proves the required cofinality: extend an open neighborhood $U_1\subset\Sigma_1$ to an ambient open $W$, then use $W\cup(\Sigma''\setminus\Sigma_1)$ as a neighborhood of $\Sigma'$. This argument does not apply to an arbitrary nonclosed trace such as a punctured complement, and an analytic-topos version must retain the intended closed-immersion interpretation.

matches.text: The admission that the reduction “ne s’explicite pas aisément, au niveau des groupoïdes fondamentaux” concerns information lost when passing from a closed immersion of topoi to its induced groupoid map. It **restates** the distinction between the mixed recollement topos and its multigaloisian reflection in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and **adds** the concrete problem of recovering open complements from that reduced data. A simple illustration is that both pairs $(\mathbb C,\{0\})$ and $(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ induce, up to equivalence, the same arrow of trivial connected fundamental groupoids, while their open complements have respectively fundamental group $\mathbb Z$ and no objects. This **adds** a non-Boolean test to the finite powerset models in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106, 116, and 128, while preserving an explicit check of the composable-pair description on scan 188. matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

matches.text: The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. Recovering a rational section from an arbitrary compatible family of abstract group splittings is a stronger existence problem and does not follow from closed-point density.

This adds a higher-dimensional local statement to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, where the kernel is identified “par Kummer” for a punctured trait. The exact sequence survives this generalization, but the assertion $I\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)$ belongs to the tame one-dimensional situation and must not be transferred to an arbitrary higher-dimensional local ring. Normality and the choices of a geometric point and compatible henselizations should therefore remain visible in any reformulation.

For a smooth curve, the punctured completion and its nonzero tangent line carry the covering-theoretic data used to define a tangential base point (Deligne, 1989, §§15.22–15.26). The statement should therefore be understood as a localization of the cusp-splitting problem, not as saying that the full global fundamental group is determined by one formal disk. The arithmetic descent data and the morphism from that local group into the global group still have to be retained.

matches.text: The desired “vue d’ensemble” can be organized by composing group homomorphisms over the arithmetic quotient, with residue-field maps supplied by decomposition groups rather than by nonexistent canonical inclusions $k(s)\subset K$. This adds a comparison between the local groupoid in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, and the conjugacy classification of splittings on scan 63 (“mod. autom. intérieurs”). For a fixed based extension, a splitting gives an actual conjugation action on its geometric kernel, whereas changing the base point or transport path changes the comparison by an inner automorphism. The latter dependence is explicit in SGA 1, Exposé XIII, §2.10, and explains why the author’s insistence on “effectives” requires compatible choices (Grothendieck, 1971/2003).

This restates the warning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, that the residue algebraic closure is not canonically the previously chosen closure of the ground field. Taking the complete regular curve model organizes its places intrinsically, but does not remove the conjugacy choice of a lift $s^{\prime}$ or supply a preferred splitting of $D_{s^{\prime}}\to G_{k(s)}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). matches.text: The conjecture “ssi il y a bonne réduction” has a precise later theorem for hyperbolic pointed curves over a discrete valuation field. Tamagawa proves that good reduction of the pair is equivalent to trivial outer inertia on one, equivalently every, prime-to-residue-characteristic pro-$\ell$ geometric fundamental group (Tamagawa, 1997, Theorem 5.3). This adds a group criterion to the marked-curve setting of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 5, with its “fini étale” boundary. In the manuscript’s residue-characteristic-zero situation, this validates the nonabelian a)–b) comparison, without validating the proposed substitutions of $H_1$ in c) and d).

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

Such a restriction should not be identified with a ramified extension of the local generic field that kills its inertia: decomposition and residue quotients distinguish those operations (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). For instance, the twist in RN103-03 becomes constant after adjoining $\sqrt t$, whereas its residual action is already geometric over $\mathbf Q$ before making any residue extension.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

matches.text: For “Ladite extension est admissible” on scan 102, the counterexample to e)$\Rightarrow$a) survives the stronger quantifier “for every splitting”: for any section $s:G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the restricted descent cocycle is the continuous quadratic character $\chi_t\circ s$. Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. Confidence is high because the argument restricts the actual geometric descent cocycle before applying fundamental groups, rather than inferring full geometricity from $H_1$.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

The Artin–Schreier cover $z^p-z=tx$ of $X_T$ gives a class in $\Omega[x]/\{h^p-h\}$ outside the image of $k[x]/\{h^p-h\}$, so the natural $\pi_1(X_T)\to\pi_1(X)$ cannot be an isomorphism although $T$ is $1$-connected (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0A3J; compare the same obstruction in Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). This **differs** from the characteristic-zero curve setting of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19–22**, and does not affect scan 106's change of the field of a base point while keeping $X$ fixed. Confidence: high, because polynomial Artin–Schreier classes detect the failure explicitly; this is an application of a known obstruction to the manuscript's wording, not a claim of a new counterexample in the literature.

matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

matches.text: For “A t-on une réciproque ?” on scan 120, take $K=\mathbf C$, $L=\mathbf C(t)$, $U=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf C}$, and the valuation at infinity on $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf C}$. Its nontrivial inertia maps trivially to $\pi_1(U)=1$, since the complex affine line is simply connected and the étale group is its profinite completion, but the unique center of the valuation on the proper model is $\infty\notin U$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Section 64.27, “Comparison,” Tag 03VD, and Lemma 58.13.5, Tag 0BUA). This **differs** from the restricted curve classes in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 20**, and is permitted by scan 115's explicit allowance for algebraically closed $K$. Confidence: high because both the trivial target group and the missing center are explicit; the example does not disprove the additional marginal restriction, and the same test can be transferred to $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Q}$ using characteristic-zero base-change invariance and the arithmetic sequence (Landesman, 2024, Theorem 1.1; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BTX).

This agrees with the modern Riemann–Zariski construction as a locally ringed inverse limit over proper birational models; normal models suffice, and regular models give the same limit when a resolution theorem supplies a cofinal family of them (Temkin, 2011, Introduction and Proposition 2.2.1). It **differs** from **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, whose projective system of group schemes is representable as a scheme because its transition maps are affine, a condition not supplied for the proper birational transitions here. For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

matches.text: At scan 122, the opening continuation of scan 121 says that codimension-one points “correspondent exactement” to the indicated finite-type “jauges”, with “ess.” versus “ext.” still marked as a reading doubt. With the manuscript's codimension $n-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(V)$, lift $n-1$ algebraically independent residue elements to $V$ and choose a normal proper model where those lifts are regular at its center: the center has codimension one, its local ring is a DVR dominated by $V$, and hence equals $V$, giving an essentially finite-type divisorial valuation ring. This **adds** the higher-dimensional residue criterion to the curve-local “anneau-jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, and agrees with the description of Zariski prime divisors by codimension-one local rings and residue transcendence degree in Pop (2006, pp. 294–295). Confidence: high in the divisorial characterization, including the converse supplied by a prime divisor on a normal model; it neither identifies all discrete valuations with divisorial ones nor resolves the abbreviated handwritten adjective.

Since $v(x)=1$, $v(y)=2$, and $y/x^2$ has residue 1 and therefore all compatible roots in the henselization, the inertia map has weights $(1,2)$, whose image has infinite index in the rank-two target. This adds a concrete contradiction to the unrestricted open-image assertion beyond the single-uniformizer model of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77, inside the elementary product-hyperbolic scope; the full $N_V\to N_x$ image is also non-open because its intersection with $I_x$ is exactly this inertia image when both residue fields are $\mathbf Q$. Confidence: high, because the Kummer characters explicitly compute the map; the target is the abstract local inertia, not an assumed global embedding, and the example does not refute the master section conjecture.

matches.text: The claim that $\hat X\setminus D$ « a un caractère invariant » should be tested by comparing the pairs or boundary maps associated with different compactifications, keeping the boundary object separate from the homotopy type of the whole complement. **Context comparison — differs in scope:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 127–133, builds a system on open strata and their normal torsors, not merely a single invariant of the open variety; cote 149’s formulation should retain that additional relative information. Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

matches.text: The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”.
