This total space retracts to $S^3$, so its fundamental group is zero, whereas the trivial punctured line bundle over $\mathbb P^1$ has fundamental group $\mathbb Z$; the contrast is the Hopf-bundle instance of the connecting map discussed by Serre (1949–1950, §§1, 5). This **adds** an explicit example to the normal-line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, and the $\pi_2$ caveat on scan 130, and tests the models on current scans 175–178 as well as the earlier qualification on scan 148. matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). matches.text: The phrase « l'action extérieure “cyclotomique” » invites a comparison between the system of maps $T^J\to\pi_{U/K}$ and the stabilizers of all roots of the boundary divisors: in characteristic zero, their geometric fibers involve $\varprojlim_n\mu_n^J$, with the arithmetic cyclotomic action and, when branches are not globally labeled, their permutation action. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, describes the corresponding integral local systems and torus torsors, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, identifies the one-branch inertia with a Tate module in its discussion of tangential splittings. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3 and Theorem 6.22) identify the relevant Kummer étale topos with that of the infinite root stack, providing a candidate precise setting for this comparison. **Our confidence: medium**, since the local stabilizers and actions agree in the characteristic-zero normal-crossing case, but this alone neither proves that their maps into a global fundamental group are injective nor recognizes all valuations from that group.

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: The extension to “une immersion locale de topos” is qualified by “sauf erreur,” so the general topos construction is not established here. It adds a new neighborhood operation to the site-independent flag axioms of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 118–119, and to the tentative topos interpretation of germ coverings in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–243. One must define the intended class of immersions and the relevant limit of localizations, then prove that composition supplies the indicated morphism of germs; the existence of slice topoi alone does not settle that neighborhood problem (Artin et al., 1972, Exposé IV, §5).

matches.text: The transvection example can be checked directly if the uncertain upper-right matrix entry is the retained first reading $1$: the generator acts by $(x,y)\mapsto(x+y,y)$ and fixes the line $y=0$. An equivariant linear section of the quotient would send $1$ to a vector $(a,1)$ fixed by the generator, but that vector is sent to $(a+1,1)$, so the tangent extension does not split and an equivariant tubular diffeomorphism inducing the prescribed normal identification cannot exist. This adds an explicit verification to the proposed descent in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 259–260, where local coordinates have no such equivariance constraint; confidence is high conditional on the entry $1$, and the calculation is a test of the author's example rather than a claim of novelty.

The phrase “seul le facteur $I_{s^{\prime}}\simeq T$” isolates the inertia left before a residual section can be chosen. This restates the splitting problem in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73 (“un torseur”), with scan 82 calling the peripheral extension trivial: split does not mean that its cyclotomic conjugation action is trivial. For an equicharacteristic-zero henselian trait, a uniformizer supplies a splitting, and its inertia-conjugacy classes form a torsor under $H^1(k,\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1))\simeq\varprojlim_n k^\times/(k^\times)^n$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). At a codimension-one zero or pole, its residue is the integer $v(h)$, so the failed nonvanishing condition leaves a calculable ramification contribution rather than a well-defined nonzero tangent vector (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. After fixing one section $s$, another has the form $s^{\prime}(g)=c(g)s(g)$ with $c$ a continuous nonabelian $1$-cocycle in $\pi$, and its action is $\operatorname{Int}(c(g))\alpha_s(g)$. Thus changing the section of (31) preserves the outer action but can change the actual action and its point-theoretic interpretation; this is a direct calculation from multiplication in the extension.

Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. Confidence is high because the argument restricts the actual geometric descent cocycle before applying fundamental groups, rather than inferring full geometricity from $H_1$.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). matches.text: The warning that generization “ne correspond à aucun morphisme” of the two punctured principal bundles makes the distinction between geometric maps and maps on covering data structural. It restates the obstruction already explicit in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 135, “mais non un morphisme entre les espaces avec $*$,” while adding a proposed solution through neighborhood germs. This also connects to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 262, which identifies the absence of a direct map between the punctured germ and the tangent-direction circle as the difficulty solved by its invariant functor; comparing these two constructions is more precise than treating generization as an ordinary map of bundles.

matches.text: The parenthetical “défini à iso unique près ?...” asks for a uniqueness statement about the neighborhood germ, and the sentence about descent to multiplicities is still exploratory. This adds an immersion-relative construction to the germ around an actual subset defined by its neighborhood filter in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and to the filter-based category of germs on scan 242. A proof needs a stated category of germs over $Y$ and an account of local branch separation: uniqueness over the ambient object is a different assertion from uniqueness of a bare germ or of a chosen tubular parametrization.

This adds a possible construction to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where the points of $D_d$ already remember a local branch germ, and to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–245, where germs and their coverings are organized by filters. Confidence is medium: the local model is explicit, but effectiveness and presentation independence for the author's multiplicities still require proof, especially in light of scan 146's equivariant obstruction to choosing a normal-bundle parametrization.

An equivariant linear section of the quotient would send $1$ to a vector $(a,1)$ fixed by the generator, but that vector is sent to $(a+1,1)$, so the tangent extension does not split and an equivariant tubular diffeomorphism inducing the prescribed normal identification cannot exist. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. Confidence: high in this distinction, medium in the intended terminology, and low in the marked subscript; it does not assert invariance of $\pi_1(X_\Omega)$ under changing the base field of $X$.

matches.text: At scan 113, manuscript page 56, continuing at the top of scan 114, “une classe d'iso. de groupes profinis sans plus, pas un groupe extérieur” warns that ambiguity comes from conjugation by the ambient group. This **restates** the extension perspective of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 71**, and **adds** an explicit warning to that file's conjugation calculations in scans 48–50. For $1\to N\to G\to Q\to 1$, ambient conjugation induces a canonical $Q\to\operatorname{Out}(N)$, because changing a lift changes its action only by an inner automorphism of $N$; retaining that action, or the whole extension, preserves information lost by the bare isomorphism class of $N$. This **restates** the pointed henselian-trait construction of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–26**, while making the conjugacy choices explicit. The fixed fields of decomposition and inertia are respectively the fraction fields of the henselization and strict henselization, so fixing the prolongation $x'$ gives the asserted embedded subgroups, whereas forgetting it leaves conjugacy classes (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.13.1, Tag 0BSW). matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

matches.text: At the end of scan 121, manuscript page 60, “ce n'est pas un schéma !” is qualified by the insertion “si $n\geq2$”, and scan 122 adds that $n=0,1$ are the only scheme cases. For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). Confidence: high under this normal finite-type model interpretation; neither the mere existence of nonnoetherian stalks nor the incorrect noetherian-stalk assertion assessed in 122-CJ1 would prove nonschematicity.

matches.text: The claim that $\hat X\setminus D$ « a un caractère invariant » should be tested by comparing the pairs or boundary maps associated with different compactifications, keeping the boundary object separate from the homotopy type of the whole complement. **Context comparison — differs in scope:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 127–133, builds a system on open strata and their normal torsors, not merely a single invariant of the open variety; cote 149’s formulation should retain that additional relative information. Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

It **adds** a general admissible-support gluing statement to the nonformal neighborhood structure anticipated in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 133, and must be distinguished from the two different gluing constructions in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166. A proof should define the comparison pseudodiagram and establish effective descent for its local branch charts, including the relevant comparison $2$-cells. Lurie’s Theorem 6.1.3.9 and Proposition 6.1.3.10 give a possible modern descent test for diagrams inside an infinity-topos, but do not identify this colimit of varying germ topoi without an additional construction (Lurie, 2009, pp. 548–549 in the updated author PDF).

This **adds** a selection of whole normalized branches to the branch-intersection construction in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 108, rather than simply pulling back a closed subset. This **adds** a closed-subset classification to the branch-labeling torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 109 and 117, where permutation monodromy is already built into the flag spaces. matches.text: The assertion that the global line “se reconstitue” as $\mathbb C^*\amalg_{\mathbb D^*}\mathbb D$ requires a precise category, because $\mathbb D$ is introduced as a germ rather than a specified open disc. It **adds** an explicit analytic local/global model to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 162–166, where the diagram of punctured neighborhoods, open part, and closed part produces both a glued topos and a distinct fundamental-groupoid topos. For a chosen open disc, the two sets $\mathbb C^*$ and $\mathbb D$ cover $\mathbb C$, so ordinary sheaf descent supplies a concrete test case; a germ formulation still needs independence under shrinking and the corresponding universal property. Passing directly from that cover to an asserted pushout of unspecified “types” would skip the principal definition that the formula leaves open.

It **adds** partially punctured neighborhood pieces to the intersection/flag combinatorics in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 113. The full nine-object product of the two three-object gluing spans records these mixed overlaps as well as $\mathbb D^*\times\mathbb D^*$, whereas the diagram for the complement of the origin omits the final bidisc piece. matches.text: The inserted phrase “fibré conormal” accompanies an exact sequence with the usual direction of a normal-bundle sequence. This **differs** from the explicit “faisceau normal” construction in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 122, while `LM_140-3_text.tex`, scan 293, shows that a check accent can also occur in the geometric-vector-bundle notation $\check V(\mathcal N)$. Under the standard convention for $Z\hookrightarrow Y\hookrightarrow X$, the conormal sequence starts with $\mathcal C_{Y/X}|_Z$, and dualizing a locally split exact sequence gives $0\to N_{Z/Y}\to N_{Z/X}\to N_{Y/X}|_Z\to0$ (Stacks Project Authors, 2026a, §37.63(4); 2026c, Lemma 31.22.6). This is a convention/readability question for the displayed symbols, not authorization to replace “conormal,” reverse arrows, or remove an accent in the transcription.

matches.text: “Forme … une stratification globale de $U$” is the needed first step before the assignment $U\mapsto\mathrm{Strat}_{\mathrm{glob}}(U)$ becomes a presheaf and can be sheafified. It **adds** an explicit local-to-global formalism to the germ constructions of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, whose locality comes from an already specified divisor. The verification must show that successive component refinements agree, retain local finiteness and the frontier and connected-germ conditions, and define the equivalence of representatives used for sections of the associated sheaf.

matches.text: The deletion of “séparé” in favour of “un faisceau,” together with the margin read uncertainly as “est connue quand on la connaît localement,” suggests that uniqueness from local data is being distinguished from existence of a global representative. This **adds** a descent question to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where an ambient global divisor already supplies the representative, and **differs** from the categorical recollement of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, which does not settle separatedness of this presheaf of partitions. The relevant question is whether connectedness forces two global partitions with the same local component data to coincide even when compatible local partitions fail to form one admissible global partition. The decisive marginal wording remains uncertain, so this is a proposed interpretation of the revision, not a corrected reading.

matches.text: The claim “contre exemple encore plus simple: les feuilletages!” needs its scope specified, since ordinary foliations of positive transverse dimension have infinitely many local plaques and are not locally finite partitions as in 181 a). The search for local equivalence relations and foliations in the supplied primary files found no matching earlier construction; the nearest germ construction, `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, instead uses a finite local branch set, so the present passage **adds** a broader analogy whose hypotheses are not supplied there. Does “feuilletages” refer to the general SGA theory of local equivalence relations invoked immediately afterwards, or to an intended wider notion of stratification? This question preserves the literal wording and does not import arbitrary foliations into the defined presheaf.

matches.text: The last line of scan 119, manuscript page 59, proposes $I_{x'}=\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I_{x'})$. This **differs** from the curve-loop situation in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 117 and 190** once a divisorial residue field has positive transcendence degree over $K$, and the explicit example in 119-O1 disproves the unrestricted formulation. Combining 119-O2 with intersection of normalizers gives the appropriate general expression $\operatorname{Norm}_{\pi_{L/K}}(I)=D\cap\pi_{L/K}$, whose quotient by $I$ can contain the geometric residue Galois group; **LM_140-3_text.tex, scan 418** also warns that a related algebraic-group self-normalizer analogy fails while its proposed profinite analogue still requires checking. Confidence: high in the counterexample and the intersection formula, with the latter context serving as a warning about categories rather than as a proof.

matches.text: At the end of scan 121, manuscript page 60, “ce n'est pas un schéma !” is qualified by the insertion “si $n\geq2$”, and scan 122 adds that $n=0,1$ are the only scheme cases. For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). Confidence: high under this normal finite-type model interpretation; neither the mere existence of nonnoetherian stalks nor the incorrect noetherian-stalk assertion assessed in 122-CJ1 would prove nonschematicity.

matches.text: For 130-O1, the characteristic-zero DVR calculation gives $I_V\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)$, whereas the two-branch local Kummer calculation gives $I_x\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)^2$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BUA; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XIII, Corollary 5.6). Since $v(x)=1$, $v(y)=2$, and $y/x^2$ has residue 1 and therefore all compatible roots in the henselization, the inertia map has weights $(1,2)$, whose image has infinite index in the rank-two target. This adds a concrete contradiction to the unrestricted open-image assertion beyond the single-uniformizer model of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77, inside the elementary product-hyperbolic scope; the full $N_V\to N_x$ image is also non-open because its intersection with $I_x$ is exactly this inertia image when both residue fields are $\mathbf Q$. Confidence: high, because the Kummer characters explicitly compute the map; the target is the abstract local inertia, not an assumed global embedding, and the example does not refute the master section conjecture.

matches.text: As a test of the general indexing, let $D_1,D_2\subset\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf P^1$ be the diagonal and the graph of $z\mapsto2z$; they meet transversely at two points. One simplex per nonempty index set produces a single edge, whereas retaining the two components of the intersection gives two edges with common endpoints and hence a circle, as in the component-indexed dual-complex definition (Payne, 2013, §2). This adds a component-counting diagnostic to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 128–129, whose flag spaces retain component data, and to the componentwise correction on 135. Confidence: high for this elementary calculation, because the two intersection points are explicit; this is not a counterexample under the later proviso that every relevant $D_J$ be contractible, which the disconnected intersection violates.

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.8 | The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. This does not identify $f_!$ with the left adjoint $f_\sharp$ of D.7. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HA 5.5.5.1; Volpe 6.9). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.13 | A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define the contravariant fully faithful functor \[ \Phi_P(F)=\mathbb V_{\|NP\|}\,E_P^{\max}(DF), \qquad F\in\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{perf}}). \tag{D.13a} \] If $f:P\to Q$ is categorically smooth, then its realization $g$ satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(f_!F)\simeq g_+\Phi_P(F). \tag{D.13b} \] Thus ordinary cosheaf pushforward realizes this specified dual of left Kan extension. The cosheaf subcategories in (D.13a) are defined as Verdier images of maximum-constructible perfect sheaves; they are not being identified with literal minimum-constructible cosheaves. For a noncommutative ring the target coefficients are modules over its opposite ring. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. |

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

This **adds** a closed-admissible-subset base-change statement to the neighborhood-filter definition in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, whose residual germs also show why an arbitrary trace cannot be identified from its center alone. At the ordinary neighborhood-filter level, closedness of $\Sigma_1\subset\Sigma''$ proves the required cofinality: extend an open neighborhood $U_1\subset\Sigma_1$ to an ambient open $W$, then use $W\cup(\Sigma''\setminus\Sigma_1)$ as a neighborhood of $\Sigma'$. This argument does not apply to an arbitrary nonclosed trace such as a punctured complement, and an analytic-topos version must retain the intended closed-immersion interpretation.

matches.text: Revisit the sphere counterexample using the later “catégorie topologique”: under the literal non-strict germ-flag topology for $\mathbb P^1=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$, the object space should be $S^2\amalg\{\infty\}$, with the identity families and one further arrow from the extra point to $\infty$ in the sphere component. Its internal nerve then realizes as $S^2$ with an interval attached at that point, which deformation retracts to $S^2$, whereas the discrete two-object incidence category realizes as an interval. This **adds** a test of retained spatial topology to the internal analytic category of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 114, and to the distinction between geometric and mixed topoi in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–168. Confidence is high in the stated interval-attachment calculation and medium in its identification with the manuscript's germ topology, which must be verified; it establishes neither a general reconstruction theorem nor an identification with an exit-path category.

matches.text: Use the drawing with “$7$” incident strata as a concrete test of the germ nerve: the planar model has a central minimum, three ray strata, and three sectors, giving seven objects, nineteen weakly ordered pairs, and thirty-seven weakly ordered triples at the centre. This **adds** a non-Boolean test to the finite powerset models in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106, 116, and 128, while preserving an explicit check of the composable-pair description on scan 188. In the corresponding finite global-chart model, the source spaces are copies of each source closure indexed by its incident chains, so finite étaleness of those projections can hold even though the poset is not Boolean; the example thus separates two properties mentioned together on scan 189. Confidence is high in the finite count and medium in transferring that global-chart topology to every local representative, and no conclusion about reconstruction of an arbitrary stratified space is drawn.

188-03 — The three-ray local poset as a finite calculation

matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

This **differs** from the normal-crossing hypothesis in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 116, and **adds** an explicit witness that the general local-stratification framework has non-Boolean incidence. The count is interpreted in the planar model as the centre, three rays, and three sectors; it does not by itself disprove the Segal identity, finite étaleness, or any particular homotopy-reconstruction assertion. A useful axiomatization should therefore keep the Boolean local-order condition separate from the categorical and topological conditions.

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.8 | The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

matches.text: The ambition to “reconstituer tous les ‘topos canoniques’ … ou leurs groupoïdes fondamentaux” must keep those two outputs distinct. It **adds** a broader reconstruction objective to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 166–168, which already distinguishes the mixed topos from its fundamental-groupoid replacement and treats acyclicity as a further question. In the current continuation, scan 179 extends the expectation to homotopy types, but scan 180 **contradicts** the unrestricted inference with $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb C}$ and one boundary point: the stated quasi-Galoisian replacement loses the nonzero degree-two cohomology of the sphere. matches.text: The emphatic “est une équivalence d’homotopie” concerns the projection of the affine torsor onto the punctured quotient bundle. It **adds** a topological conclusion to the affine-translation distinction in `LM_140-3_text.tex`, scans 294 and 299. For an actual locally trivial affine bundle over a paracompact analytic-manifold base, a partition of unity combines local affine sections into a continuous section, and affine interpolation contracts each fiber toward it, giving a direct proof without requiring a holomorphic splitting. The remaining obligation is to identify the manuscript objects with such bundles before transporting this argument to a germ or topos model.

matches.text: “Si $X$ est compact” is used to obtain finitely many intrinsic strata, “qui sont loc. compactes,” with the warning that finiteness need not survive restriction to an open set. This **adds** a global finiteness conclusion to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where finiteness concerns branch sets at individual points, not the number of global strata. A proof can try a finite cover by charts with finitely many local pieces, but must justify that each local connected piece belongs to one globally constructed stratum; local compactness additionally requires the relevant separation convention and locally closed chart models. These are separate checks, and neither follows simply from finiteness of the local incidence posets.

This **generalizes** the analytic internal-category data in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 114, where identities, composition, associativity, and units are explicitly listed, to the newly constructed topological germ spaces. matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

matches.text: The assertion that “$D=S\setminus S^{\prime}$ est purement de codim $1$” follows if the rational map extends to the compactification and the pulled-back boundary equation remains a non-zero-divisor. In that situation the inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor, hence has pure codimension one; the local pullback condition is essential (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01WQ). This adds a global divisor interpretation to the “indice de ramification” discussed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 45. The parenthesis about $g\geq1$ or a one-dimensional base should therefore be kept as part of the author’s extension argument, rather than treating purity as a property of every indeterminacy locus on an arbitrary higher-dimensional base.

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

matches.text: The question “qu’attendre d’une telle action ?” can first be separated into its formal and geometric parts. It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. After fixing one section $s$, another has the form $s^{\prime}(g)=c(g)s(g)$ with $c$ a continuous nonabelian $1$-cocycle in $\pi$, and its action is $\operatorname{Int}(c(g))\alpha_s(g)$. Thus changing the section of (31) preserves the outer action but can change the actual action and its point-theoretic interpretation; this is a direct calculation from multiplication in the extension.

This restates the “maquette” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 11, and adds an arithmetic question to the three boundary partitions of the four-pointed line on scan 61. Independent node-smoothing parameters give local boundary directions, while the graph distinguishes a separating node from a loop contributing to the Jacobian’s toric part (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5 and Lemma 1.17). Consequently the graph supplies useful test cases for the conjectural equivalences without itself determining the entire arithmetic outer action.

matches.text: The insertion “ou un” is justified, provided a splitting of (31) exists and the assertion means that its $T$-action is inner. The geometric hyperbolic group is center-free, so $\pi\simeq\operatorname{Inn}(\pi)$ identifies an inner-valued action of $T$ with a continuous homomorphism $T\to\pi$ (Tamagawa, 1997, Proposition 1.11). This restates the distinction between splittings and kernel conjugacy in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63: the outer restriction is independent of the selected lift. It does not assert that the resulting homomorphism $T\to\pi$ is zero, and an existential “one splitting” should not be replaced by a vacuous universal statement when no splitting is available.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: The invitation “Le cas du genre $0$” has an explicit editorial test: $U=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q((t))}\setminus\{0,t,1,\infty\}$ has all four punctures rational and $H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbf Z_\ell)\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell(1)^3$, so its $t$-adic inertia acts trivially for every $\ell$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

matches.text: At scan 122, the opening continuation of scan 121 says that codimension-one points “correspondent exactement” to the indicated finite-type “jauges”, with “ess.” versus “ext.” still marked as a reading doubt. With the manuscript's codimension $n-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(V)$, lift $n-1$ algebraically independent residue elements to $V$ and choose a normal proper model where those lifts are regular at its center: the center has codimension one, its local ring is a DVR dominated by $V$, and hence equals $V$, giving an essentially finite-type divisorial valuation ring. This **adds** the higher-dimensional residue criterion to the curve-local “anneau-jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, and agrees with the description of Zariski prime divisors by codimension-one local rings and residue transcendence degree in Pop (2006, pp. 294–295). Confidence: high in the divisorial characterization, including the converse supplied by a prime divisor on a normal model; it neither identifies all discrete valuations with divisorial ones nor resolves the abbreviated handwritten adjective.

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. matches.text: The claim that the “donnée … est équivalente” to compatible subsets of $\pi_0(D_d)$ makes the admissible closed $\Sigma$ recoverable from the global component data rather than arbitrary local labels. This **adds** a closed-subset classification to the branch-labeling torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 109 and 117, where permutation monodromy is already built into the flag spaces. To prove both directions one must show that the component selections respect the incidence maps and descend to a locally finite union of branch intersections, and that every such union yields exactly those selections. Working with $\pi_0(D_d)$ incorporates the global branch identifications; independently labeling local branches without their transport could produce a selection that does not descend.

The induced ring $V=L\cap\mathbf Q[[t]]$ has value group $\mathbf Z$, since $v(x)=1$, and residue field $\mathbf Q$, hence is a DVR centered at $(0,0)$ on $X=(\mathbf P^1)^2$ with elementary anabelian open $U=(\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. This adds a nondivisorial DVR test to the jauges of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; see 130-O2 for the noetherian-stalk consequence and 130-O3 for its inertia map. Confidence: high, because injectivity of the field embedding, the value group, and the residue field follow directly from the construction and the DVR criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 00I8).

matches.text: The warning that generization “ne correspond à aucun morphisme” of the two punctured principal bundles makes the distinction between geometric maps and maps on covering data structural. It restates the obstruction already explicit in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 135, “mais non un morphisme entre les espaces avec $*$,” while adding a proposed solution through neighborhood germs. This also connects to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 262, which identifies the absence of a direct map between the punctured germ and the tangent-direction circle as the difficulty solved by its invariant functor; comparing these two constructions is more precise than treating generization as an ordinary map of bundles.

matches.text: The parenthetical “défini à iso unique près ?...” asks for a uniqueness statement about the neighborhood germ, and the sentence about descent to multiplicities is still exploratory. This adds an immersion-relative construction to the germ around an actual subset defined by its neighborhood filter in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and to the filter-based category of germs on scan 242. A proof needs a stated category of germs over $Y$ and an account of local branch separation: uniqueness over the ambient object is a different assertion from uniqueness of a bare germ or of a chosen tubular parametrization.

matches.text: For the proposed construction “par descente,” a concrete route would be to attach to each local embedded chart of $D'\to Y$ its cofiltered system of neighborhoods and then descend that system, retaining the transition isomorphisms on overlapping charts. This adds a possible construction to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where the points of $D_d$ already remember a local branch germ, and to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–245, where germs and their coverings are organized by filters. Confidence is medium: the local model is explicit, but effectiveness and presentation independence for the author's multiplicities still require proof, especially in light of scan 146's equivariant obstruction to choosing a normal-bundle parametrization.

matches.text: The extension to “une immersion locale de topos” is qualified by “sauf erreur,” so the general topos construction is not established here. It adds a new neighborhood operation to the site-independent flag axioms of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 118–119, and to the tentative topos interpretation of germ coverings in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–243. One must define the intended class of immersions and the relevant limit of localizations, then prove that composition supplies the indicated morphism of germs; the existence of slice topoi alone does not settle that neighborhood problem (Artin et al., 1972, Exposé IV, §5).

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

matches.text: The author now says that “croisements normaux” serves to express the germ groupoids in simpler terms, separating existence of generization from its torus description. This qualifies the formulation in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 133, where the missing half-simplicial structure was said to require normal-intersection hypotheses, while it develops the branch-torsor constructions of scans 121–123. In a local chart with $r$ coordinate branches, the complement has the meridians of $(\mathbb C^*)^r$; the remaining problem is descent with branch permutations and global twisting, not merely identifying each local fundamental group with $\mathbb Z^r$.

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

A local proof should track every coordinate hyperplane and then show that the compatible local models descend with the branch-permutation torsor; ordinary homotopy equivalence of the unpunctured spaces does not supply this condition.

It adds a covering-extension claim to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 136–137, where the starred locus and its local embedding are described but this equivalence is not proved. The task is to show both extension and full faithfulness for coverings across the omitted deeper loci in the germ, with the topology and puncturing fixed; merely noting that the base inclusion is dense does not justify either property.

It qualifies the extension description in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 130–131, where the margin already warns that the full lattice kernel requires a condition on $\pi_2$. The connecting homomorphism can kill meridians, so a proof should identify its image and the induced local-system action rather than assert an injection of the entire lattice; the fibration exact sequence is the relevant classical result (Serre, 1949–1950, §1).

matches.text: A useful test of “un quotient de $T$” and “par l’image des $\pi_2$” is the zero-section divisor in the total space of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$: its punctured normal bundle identifies with $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$ by sending a nonzero vector in its tautological line to that vector. This total space retracts to $S^3$, so its fundamental group is zero, whereas the trivial punctured line bundle over $\mathbb P^1$ has fundamental group $\mathbb Z$; the contrast is the Hopf-bundle instance of the connecting map discussed by Serre (1949–1950, §§1, 5). This **adds** an explicit example to the normal-line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, and the $\pi_2$ caveat on scan 130, and tests the models on current scans 175–178 as well as the earlier qualification on scan 148. Confidence is high in the calculation because the identification is explicit, and medium in its usefulness for the full diagram comparison because one piece does not settle canonical transition maps; no claim is made that this particular bundle occurs in the moduli application.

This restates geometrically the branch-germ space defined in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, and differs from the purely site-theoretic flag axioms on scans 114–119. The point to settle is what replaces analytic normalization in the purely topological normal-crossing setting: separating local branches is a candidate operation, but its topology, local immersion property, and behavior under monodromy require an explicit construction.

matches.text: “On applique le th.” proposes a recursive application of boundary gluing to every flag space, with the new flags obtained by appending the fixed flag $\delta$. This **restates** the induced normal-crossing deployment on $D_d$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 127, and **adds** the corresponding assertion for a whole flag and its punctured-neighborhood topos. A proof should identify the deployment induced on $D_\delta$ with the displayed extended-flag diagram, including its face maps and the comparison to $V^*_{\Theta_\delta,D_\delta}$; the earlier text explicitly declines to develop the induced construction, so that reduction has not yet been supplied in the cited passages.

matches.text: The assertion that an “analyse locale facile” of the type of a purity theorem permits one to “négliger $\Theta^{(3)}$” is the missing geometric input in the two-level formula. It **adds** an invariance assertion for the fundamental groupoid of the punctured boundary to the local branch-intersection model in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 106, and the purified skeleton construction in that file, scan 137. The needed argument concerns the comparison of the corresponding boundary germs after removal of the higher skeleton, including components and loops; invariance of a smooth ambient space under deleting a high-codimension subset alone would not identify that comparison. No occurrence of “pureté” was found in the supplied primary context, and this sentence supplies neither the local calculation nor a higher-homotopy invariance claim.

It **adds** this collapse to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131 and 133, which distinguish the partially functorial ordinary stratum groupoids from the proposed semisimplicial system of punctured-normal groupoids. A complete proof must specify the colimit convention and the comparison functor, then show that removing the higher strata and replacing the surviving diagram preserve the relevant fundamental groupoid; the objectwise descriptions of the $\widetilde\Pi$'s do not by themselves establish that conclusion. The formula targets the boundary $V^*_{\Theta,X}$, and scan 156 explicitly explains why such a formula can contain no ambient-space reconstruction in the curve case.

matches.text: The hypothesis “$X^{*\infty}\longrightarrow X^*$” is a $1$-equivalence, but the conclusion is written $\Pi_1X$, without a star. That conclusion **differs** from the distinction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 168–169, between a punctured space and the quotient of its fundamental group obtained by filling holes; the hypothesis as written supplies the groupoid of $X^*$. Scan 156 expressly separates $\Pi_1(X)$ from $\Pi_1(X^*)$ and introduces an additional gluing leg, making a missing star in (247) a plausible reading question rather than an authorized correction. matches.text: The second version asserts that the semisimplicial family of germ topoi has colimit “équivalente canoniquement” to $V^*_{\Sigma,X}$, but gives no descent proof. It **adds** a general admissible-support gluing statement to the nonformal neighborhood structure anticipated in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 133, and must be distinguished from the two different gluing constructions in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166. A proof should define the comparison pseudodiagram and establish effective descent for its local branch charts, including the relevant comparison $2$-cells. Lurie’s Theorem 6.1.3.9 and Proposition 6.1.3.10 give a possible modern descent test for diagrams inside an infinity-topos, but do not identify this colimit of varying germ topoi without an additional construction (Lurie, 2009, pp. 548–549 in the updated author PDF).

The criticism **differs** from reading the preceding theorem as ambient reconstruction and **restates** the separate need for “bouchage de trous” in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 168. The new contribution is the explicit demand to add the open complement and the unpunctured neighborhoods to the construction. It **restates** the cospan and hole-filling construction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 162 and 168, with the closed-point groupoids now discrete. For an actual open tubular-neighborhood cover, Brown’s Theorem 3.4 proves the fundamental-groupoid pushout using an object set meeting every component of the overlap, so disconnected punctured neighborhoods cause no problem (Brown, 1967, pp. 391–392). Passage from those actual neighborhoods to the manuscript’s germ topoi still requires the relevant fundamental-groupoid comparison; the theorem does not assert an equivalence of topoi.

matches.text: The right-hand “groupoïde discret” makes the new leg kill the loop around each missing point, so after choosing paths to a basepoint the proposed formula becomes the quotient of $\pi_1(X\setminus\Theta)$ by the normal closure of the meridians. This **restates**, in the complex-curve case, the explicit quotient by the normal subgroup generated by the images of $\ker\sigma_i$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 169. Brown’s groupoid relations also provide this calculation under the open-cover hypotheses (Brown, 1967, Corollary 3.6, p. 393). Keeping the transport paths or the groupoid formulation is necessary to interpret the meridians consistently when the divisor has several points.

It **adds** a demand for the meridian-killing leg to the earlier generization formalism, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, already distinguishes an actual open-neighborhood inclusion from a map factored through the closed stratum and retains a noninvertible comparison transformation. These are different types of data: the right leg of (254) is a functor of fundamental groupoids, whereas the transformation $\alpha$ belongs to the richer topos recollement. Recovering the former therefore does not justify replacing the latter by an isomorphism when constructing all the desired topoi.

It **adds** these relative targets to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131–135, which already explains why the ordinary stratum groupoids alone lack the face maps needed for full simplicial variation. The parenthetical willingness to add missing structure is essential, since a list of the existing groupoids has not been asserted to determine the extra morphisms. Scan 160 reiterates that the reduction is difficult at the groupoid level, so this passage remains a proposed program rather than a consequence already established by the boundary theorem.

matches.text: The identity for the “trace de $\Sigma_1$” asserts that restricting the neighborhood germ of $\Sigma'$ in $\Sigma''$ to $\Sigma_1$ gives the germ of $\Sigma'\cap\Sigma_1$ in $\Sigma_1$, without requiring $\Sigma'\subset\Sigma_1$. This **adds** a closed-admissible-subset base-change statement to the neighborhood-filter definition in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, whose residual germs also show why an arbitrary trace cannot be identified from its center alone. At the ordinary neighborhood-filter level, closedness of $\Sigma_1\subset\Sigma''$ proves the required cofinality: extend an open neighborhood $U_1\subset\Sigma_1$ to an ambient open $W$, then use $W\cup(\Sigma''\setminus\Sigma_1)$ as a neighborhood of $\Sigma'$. This argument does not apply to an arbitrary nonclosed trace such as a punctured complement, and an analytic-topos version must retain the intended closed-immersion interpretation.

This **restates** the residual-germ distinction in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and **adds** the explicit comparison between $V_{\Sigma',X}^{\Sigma'}$ and $V_{\varnothing,X\setminus\Sigma'}$. For a nonempty smooth divisor, the former retains punctured tubular approach data while the latter is the empty topos, so the two operations cannot be interchanged in the proposed reduction. The example gives a useful test for every subsequent notation change involving a removed admissible subset.

It **differs** from `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 126 and 133, which expressly assign a nonformal role to normal-crossing neighborhood geometry in constructing the complete generization system. Current scans 189–190 later isolate global finite étaleness, manifold strata, and Boolean branch incidence as special properties, while reserving local triviality for tubular constructions. Read as a statement about the formal incidence category, the remark has a narrower plausible meaning; read as preserving every geometric property of the earlier construction under restriction, it remains unsupported by the passages cited.

matches.text: “Il suffit en principe” asks for functorial germ topoi $V_{\Sigma',\Sigma''}$ and transition morphisms for inclusions of pairs. This **restates** the filter-compatible morphism criterion and composition law in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 242, and **adds** the demand to express those maps through the elementary flag pieces. For ordinary inclusions of pairs, pulling back a neighborhood of the larger center gives a neighborhood of the smaller center, providing the underlying morphism of neighborhood germs. What remains to be constructed is the compatible presentation of these maps and their composites in the chosen topos diagram, rather than just their existence on underlying filters.

This adds a group criterion to the marked-curve setting of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 5, with its “fini étale” boundary. matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

Confidence is high because the coordinate change and descent cocycle are explicit; this is an editorial counterexample with finite nontrivial inertia, and no extra semistability assumption is being inserted into the manuscript.

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. heading_path: Research notes: MPL 147, scans 138–190

matches.text: The warning that generization “ne correspond à aucun morphisme” of the two punctured principal bundles makes the distinction between geometric maps and maps on covering data structural. It restates the obstruction already explicit in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 135, “mais non un morphisme entre les espaces avec $*$,” while adding a proposed solution through neighborhood germs. This also connects to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 262, which identifies the absence of a direct map between the punctured germ and the tangent-direction circle as the difficulty solved by its invariant functor; comparing these two constructions is more precise than treating generization as an ordinary map of bundles.
heading_path: Research notes: MPL 147, scans 138–190

138-05 — Scan 140, l. 11 — unpursued implication

matches.text: The parenthetical “défini à iso unique près ?...” asks for a uniqueness statement about the neighborhood germ, and the sentence about descent to multiplicities is still exploratory. This adds an immersion-relative construction to the germ around an actual subset defined by its neighborhood filter in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and to the filter-based category of germs on scan 242. A proof needs a stated category of germs over $Y$ and an account of local branch separation: uniqueness over the ambient object is a different assertion from uniqueness of a bare germ or of a chosen tubular parametrization.
heading_path: Research notes: MPL 147, scans 138–190

matches.text: For the proposed construction “par descente,” a concrete route would be to attach to each local embedded chart of $D'\to Y$ its cofiltered system of neighborhoods and then descend that system, retaining the transition isomorphisms on overlapping charts. This adds a possible construction to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where the points of $D_d$ already remember a local branch germ, and to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–245, where germs and their coverings are organized by filters. Confidence is medium: the local model is explicit, but effectiveness and presentation independence for the author's multiplicities still require proof, especially in light of scan 146's equivariant obstruction to choosing a normal-bundle parametrization.

matches.text: The extension to “une immersion locale de topos” is qualified by “sauf erreur,” so the general topos construction is not established here. It adds a new neighborhood operation to the site-independent flag axioms of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 118–119, and to the tentative topos interpretation of germ coverings in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–243. One must define the intended class of immersions and the relevant limit of localizations, then prove that composition supplies the indicated morphism of germs; the existence of slice topoi alone does not settle that neighborhood problem (Artin et al., 1972, Exposé IV, §5).

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

This adds a stronger comparison to the normal-torsor definitions on `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–127, and to the locally immersed flag geometry on scans 135–137. A proof must handle those deeper intersections and demonstrate an equivalence of the appropriate covering categories, not just compute a meridian group at a single smooth boundary point; scan 147's marginal reduction to $D'^{*}$ is itself a further assertion needing justification.

matches.text: The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.
