matches.text: “On a oublié de préciser” records an additional condition: the tubular map must carry the relevant divisor complement to the punctured normal-bundle locus. This adds a compatibility requirement to the punctured line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–126, and explains why an arbitrary smooth tubular neighborhood cannot by itself prove (239). A local proof should track every coordinate hyperplane and then show that the compatible local models descend with the branch-permutation torsor; ordinary homotopy equivalence of the unpunctured spaces does not supply this condition.

This differs from the definition $\widetilde\Pi_{\Delta_r}=\Pi_1P^*_{\Delta_r}$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 131, while retaining the missing-generization objective of scans 133–135. The change may remove a comparison theorem from the construction, but it transfers the proof obligation to the claimed extension structure and to the compatibility of its lattice quotients; the note records this as the author's proposed reorganization, not as an established equivalence of frameworks.

It adds a descent theorem to the half-simplicial groupoid programme in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131–135, and is stronger than the fundamental-group calculations associated with gluing in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–169. A proof must specify the categorical colimit, establish effective descent for sheaves along the augmented flag system, and explain how the local normal-crossing models cover the boundary germ; a comparison of $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ alone proves less than the stated theorem.

matches.text: The repeated demand for generization and a “structure d'extension” has a concrete application to the earlier programme of recovering the moduli groupoids and their graph operations. These pages add geometric machinery to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 104, which asks to determine $\Pi_1M_{g,I}$, the extensions $S\Pi_1M_G$, and the maps induced by graph generization, and to scans 78–89, where those extensions are already organized around boundary germs. A useful comparison would track a single node-smoothing meridian through the normal torsor, the punctured germ, and the graph-generization map, checking its orientation, kernel, and permutation action before asserting that the abstract gluing construction realizes the full earlier programme.

matches.text: A possible multivariable analogue of the curve construction is to use products of sufficiently small angular sectors in the normal directions and their cofiltered neighborhood germs, then descend along permutations of the branches. This adds an unmade link between the contractible cone-neighborhood filters in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 256–260, and the branch-permutation torsors in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–126. Confidence is medium: the local coordinate model supplies simply connected sectors and compatible inclusions, but independence under changes of normal-crossing charts, compatibility for nested flags, and descent over the whole base remain genuine proof obligations.

matches.text: The assertion that a suitable normal immersion is an “équivalence d'homotopie” is explicitly restricted in the margin to ordinary analytic spaces. A proof should specify whether it compares chosen sufficiently small representatives, pro-homotopy types of neighborhood systems, or topoi, and should produce compatible contractions after shrinking; that unpunctured assertion must then be separated from the stronger divisor-compatible punctured comparison added on scan 147.

heading_path: Research notes: MPL 147, scans 138–190

matches.text: “On applique le th.” proposes a recursive application of boundary gluing to every flag space, with the new flags obtained by appending the fixed flag $\delta$. This **restates** the induced normal-crossing deployment on $D_d$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 127, and **adds** the corresponding assertion for a whole flag and its punctured-neighborhood topos. A proof should identify the deployment induced on $D_\delta$ with the displayed extended-flag diagram, including its face maps and the comparison to $V^*_{\Theta_\delta,D_\delta}$; the earlier text explicitly declines to develop the induced construction, so that reduction has not yet been supplied in the cited passages.

matches.text: The same “structure à l’$\infty$” appears first as $D_\delta^{*\infty}$ and later as $D_\delta^*$, while the opening parenthesis also describes the structure at infinity of $D_\delta^{*\infty}$. The distinction **differs** from the consistently separate roles of the open stratum $D_d^*$ and its punctured normal torsor $P_d^*$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 123, and **adds** a question about missing or repeated infinity notation rather than evidence that those objects are equivalent. Scan 152, line 32, explicitly imposes an additional $1$-equivalence hypothesis before identifying a boundary with its open ambient complement, so the frozen expressions on 151 should not silently license such an identification.

matches.text: The hypothesis “$X^{*\infty}\longrightarrow X^*$” is a $1$-equivalence, but the conclusion is written $\Pi_1X$, without a star. That conclusion **differs** from the distinction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 168–169, between a punctured space and the quotient of its fundamental group obtained by filling holes; the hypothesis as written supplies the groupoid of $X^*$. Scan 156 expressly separates $\Pi_1(X)$ from $\Pi_1(X^*)$ and introduces an additional gluing leg, making a missing star in (247) a plausible reading question rather than an authorized correction. Neither this hypothesis nor (246) implies reconstruction of the full homotopy type, as the later example on scan 180 also demonstrates.

matches.text: Replacing the deleted “l’image inverse de $\Sigma$” by the union of connected components of $D_i$ that map into $\Sigma$ is a substantive definition of admissibility data. This **adds** a selection of whole normalized branches to the branch-intersection construction in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 108, rather than simply pulling back a closed subset. For two transverse branches with $\Sigma$ equal to one branch, the full inverse image in $D_1$ also contains the intersection point on the other normalized branch, whereas the revised definition selects only the component lying wholly in $\Sigma$. The assertion that these component selections recover every admissible $\Sigma$ needs the local branch model and the fact that the selected images form the required closed union.

Face compatibility requires the closure condition of (251) when the last vertex is removed and the earlier composition maps when an interior vertex is removed. This **adds** a closed-subset classification to the branch-labeling torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 109 and 117, where permutation monodromy is already built into the flag spaces. To prove both directions one must show that the component selections respect the incidence maps and descend to a locally finite union of branch intersections, and that every such union yields exactly those selections. Working with $\pi_0(D_d)$ incorporates the global branch identifications; independently labeling local branches without their transport could produce a selection that does not descend.

matches.text: The second version asserts that the semisimplicial family of germ topoi has colimit “équivalente canoniquement” to $V^*_{\Sigma,X}$, but gives no descent proof. It **adds** a general admissible-support gluing statement to the nonformal neighborhood structure anticipated in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 133, and must be distinguished from the two different gluing constructions in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166. A proof should define the comparison pseudodiagram and establish effective descent for its local branch charts, including the relevant comparison $2$-cells. Lurie’s Theorem 6.1.3.9 and Proposition 6.1.3.10 give a possible modern descent test for diagrams inside an infinity-topos, but do not identify this colimit of varying germ topoi without an additional construction (Lurie, 2009, pp. 548–549 in the updated author PDF).

matches.text: The phrase “c’est donc un crible” suggests checking admissible supports and all selected flags by finite incidence calculations in a branch chart, then imposing invariance under branch transport. This proposal **adds** a computational use to the Boolean branch poset and its permutation torsor in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106, 109, and 116: choose local intersections, close the selection under incoming arrows, and retain precisely the flags whose final vertex is selected. Confidence is high for the finite local calculation because the branch poset and the closure rule are explicit; confidence in a global implementation is conditional on correctly retaining monodromy and the analytic component data. This is a suggested consistency check and construction procedure, not a claim of novelty or a proof of the topos gluing theorem.

matches.text: Calling the previous theorem “une pure tautologie” for a smooth divisor on a curve identifies a precise limitation: the punctured boundary is just the disjoint collection of punctured point-neighborhoods. The criticism **differs** from reading the preceding theorem as ambient reconstruction and **restates** the separate need for “bouchage de trous” in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 168. The new contribution is the explicit demand to add the open complement and the unpunctured neighborhoods to the construction. Scans 159–160 continue to treat this enlargement as a program, and scan 180 prevents interpreting its fundamental-groupoid formulation as an automatic recovery of all homotopy information.

matches.text: The assertion expressing “$\Pi_1(X)$ … comme somme amalgamée” is the curve case of gluing the complement to genuine neighborhoods of the missing points. It **restates** the cospan and hole-filling construction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 162 and 168, with the closed-point groupoids now discrete. For an actual open tubular-neighborhood cover, Brown’s Theorem 3.4 proves the fundamental-groupoid pushout using an object set meeting every component of the overlap, so disconnected punctured neighborhoods cause no problem (Brown, 1967, pp. 391–392). Passage from those actual neighborhoods to the manuscript’s germ topoi still requires the relevant fundamental-groupoid comparison; the theorem does not assert an equivalence of topoi.

matches.text: The deleted remark that the right arrow “n’a pas encore reçu droit de cité” records a deficiency that survives in the live request to introduce the missing structural elements. It **adds** a demand for the meridian-killing leg to the earlier generization formalism, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, already distinguishes an actual open-neighborhood inclusion from a map factored through the closed stratum and retains a noninvertible comparison transformation. These are different types of data: the right leg of (254) is a functor of fundamental groupoids, whereas the transformation $\alpha$ belongs to the richer topos recollement. Recovering the former therefore does not justify replacing the latter by an isomorphism when constructing all the desired topoi.

matches.text: “On veut pouvoir exprimer” the groupoids of $\Sigma$, $\Sigma'\setminus\Sigma$, and relative punctured neighborhoods proposes a reconstruction program from both the $\Pi_{\Delta_r}$ and the $\widetilde\Pi_{\Delta_r}$. It **adds** these relative targets to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131–135, which already explains why the ordinary stratum groupoids alone lack the face maps needed for full simplicial variation. The parenthetical willingness to add missing structure is essential, since a list of the existing groupoids has not been asserted to determine the extra morphisms. Scan 160 reiterates that the reduction is difficult at the groupoid level, so this passage remains a proposed program rather than a consequence already established by the boundary theorem.

151-20 — Scan 157 — MPL_147_138-190_scan157.tex, lines 5–18, (255) — conjecture

matches.text: The identity for the “trace de $\Sigma_1$” asserts that restricting the neighborhood germ of $\Sigma'$ in $\Sigma''$ to $\Sigma_1$ gives the germ of $\Sigma'\cap\Sigma_1$ in $\Sigma_1$, without requiring $\Sigma'\subset\Sigma_1$. This **adds** a closed-admissible-subset base-change statement to the neighborhood-filter definition in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, whose residual germs also show why an arbitrary trace cannot be identified from its center alone. At the ordinary neighborhood-filter level, closedness of $\Sigma_1\subset\Sigma''$ proves the required cofinality: extend an open neighborhood $U_1\subset\Sigma_1$ to an ambient open $W$, then use $W\cup(\Sigma''\setminus\Sigma_1)$ as a neighborhood of $\Sigma'$. This argument does not apply to an arbitrary nonclosed trace such as a punctured complement, and an analytic-topos version must retain the intended closed-immersion interpretation.

matches.text: “Qu’on se gardera de confondre” separates removal after forming a neighborhood germ from removal of the center before that germ is formed. This **restates** the residual-germ distinction in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and **adds** the explicit comparison between $V_{\Sigma',X}^{\Sigma'}$ and $V_{\varnothing,X\setminus\Sigma'}$. For a nonempty smooth divisor, the former retains punctured tubular approach data while the latter is the empty topos, so the two operations cannot be interchanged in the proposed reduction. The example gives a useful test for every subsequent notation change involving a removed admissible subset.

The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

The isomorphism $(X,Y)\mapsto(tX,t^{3/2}Y)$ over $K(\sqrt t)$ has descent cocycle $[-1]$, so inertia acts as $-1$ on $H_1$ and rules out good reduction, whereas the uniformizer-based residue splitting fixing $\sqrt t$ pulls the full outer action back to that of $U_0/\mathbf Q$ (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). The current passage adds a reduction implication to the realization meaning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410; this example disproves that addition using the local splitting construction of scan 75. This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

Since $v(x)=1$, $v(y)=2$, and $y/x^2$ has residue 1 and therefore all compatible roots in the henselization, the inertia map has weights $(1,2)$, whose image has infinite index in the rank-two target. This adds a concrete contradiction to the unrestricted open-image assertion beyond the single-uniformizer model of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77, inside the elementary product-hyperbolic scope; the full $N_V\to N_x$ image is also non-open because its intersection with $I_x$ is exactly this inertia image when both residue fields are $\mathbf Q$. Confidence: high, because the Kummer characters explicitly compute the map; the target is the abstract local inertia, not an assumed global embedding, and the example does not refute the master section conjecture.

matches.text: | BISITE D.2 | A complete realization theorem for finite Alexandrov bases. Let $P$ be a finite poset with the topology of downsets. There are equivalences \[ (\mathrm{Top}/P)[(W^{\mathrm{opn}}_P)^{-1}] \simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal S) \simeq\operatorname{CoShv}(P;\mathcal S). \tag{D.2} \] The first equivalence sends $f:X\to P$ to the covariant diagram $p\mapsto\Pi f^{-1}(P_{\leq p})$. It includes arbitrary, possibly empty fibres and non-Hausdorff total spaces. For a discrete, possibly infinite base $P$ the same statement holds by decomposition into its open fibres. | claim (return: Proved) | Proved in outline: the adjunction `D ⊣ E`, the continuity of the jump homotopy on both kinds of generators and the induction on downsets followed; the rectification step is HTT 4.2.4.4. |

matches.text: | BISITE D.5 | Local product maps preserve the open-test class. Suppose $g:Z\to Y$ is locally a projection: each point of $Z$ has an open neighbourhood isomorphic over an open $V\subseteq Y$ to $V\times K\to V$, with $K$ a topological space. Then strict pullback along $g$ sends $W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Y$ to $W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Z$. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. |

matches.text: | BISITE D.6 | Proper base change is a coefficient theorem. Consider a cartesian square of locally compact Hausdorff spaces \[ \begin{array}{ccc} X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\[-2pt] {\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\[-2pt] Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y. \end{array} \] If $f$ is proper, the canonical mate $g^*f_*\to f'_*g'^*$ is an equivalence on sheaves of spaces. It is also an equivalence on sheaves with values in a stable bicomplete infinity-category. These are ordinary infinity-sheaves; hypercompletion is not silently substituted. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HTT 7.3.1.18; Volpe). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |
heading_path: Statements our returns make that Book V meets, each with its status (12 Nov 2026)

matches.text: | BISITE D.8 | The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. This does not identify $f_!$ with the left adjoint $f_\sharp$ of D.7. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HA 5.5.5.1; Volpe 6.9). |

For finite posets equipped with their least-vertex models, closed cosieve inclusions and product projections have topological direct images equal to their categorical right Kan extensions for space, spectrum, and derived-ring coefficients. A sieve is represented by the open complement of the complementary cosieve, rather than in general by the inclusion of its own nerve. matches.text: | BISITE D.11 | The realization comparison for every proper map of finite posets. Let $f:P\to Q$ be a $W_\infty$-proper map of finite posets. Equivalently, for every $p\in P$ and $q\geq f(p)$ the outgoing lifting poset \[ L(p,q)=\{r\in P:r\geq p,\ f(r)=q\} \tag{D.11a} \] is weakly contractible. With the minimum stratifications, the topological direct image $\|Nf\|_*$ preserves constructibility and identifies with the categorical $f_*$, including its adjunction data. This holds for spaces, spectra, and the derived category of modules over any ring. Thus the requested geometric class contains the realizations of all such proper functors, with the specified constructibility property, although mere topological properness does not suffice by D.9. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. matches.text: | BISITE D.13 | A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define the contravariant fully faithful functor \[ \Phi_P(F)=\mathbb V_{\|NP\|}\,E_P^{\max}(DF), \qquad F\in\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{perf}}). \tag{D.13a} \] If $f:P\to Q$ is categorically smooth, then its realization $g$ satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(f_!F)\simeq g_+\Phi_P(F). \tag{D.13b} \] Thus ordinary cosheaf pushforward realizes this specified dual of left Kan extension. The cosheaf subcategories in (D.13a) are defined as Verdier images of maximum-constructible perfect sheaves; they are not being identified with literal minimum-constructible cosheaves. For a noncommutative ring the target coefficients are modules over its opposite ring. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. |

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: Grothendieck announces a “morphisme canonique (dit ‘de générisation’)” and postpones its construction. The assertion adds a geometric mechanism to the expressly “non-formel” missing first-face map in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 133–135, where only the maps preserving the first flag element had been constructed. A proof must produce the functor on covering categories, show that it is independent of the tubular choices, and verify its compatibility with the already defined face and degeneracy maps; the curve construction of Deligne (1989, §§15.3–15.7) provides a precise comparison case, not a proof of the full flag statement.

matches.text: The warning that generization “ne correspond à aucun morphisme” of the two punctured principal bundles makes the distinction between geometric maps and maps on covering data structural. It restates the obstruction already explicit in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 135, “mais non un morphisme entre les espaces avec $*$,” while adding a proposed solution through neighborhood germs. This also connects to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 262, which identifies the absence of a direct map between the punctured germ and the tangent-direction circle as the difficulty solved by its invariant functor; comparing these two constructions is more precise than treating generization as an ordinary map of bundles.

matches.text: For the proposed construction “par descente,” a concrete route would be to attach to each local embedded chart of $D'\to Y$ its cofiltered system of neighborhoods and then descend that system, retaining the transition isomorphisms on overlapping charts. This adds a possible construction to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where the points of $D_d$ already remember a local branch germ, and to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–245, where germs and their coverings are organized by filters. Confidence is medium: the local model is explicit, but effectiveness and presentation independence for the author's multiplicities still require proof, especially in light of scan 146's equivariant obstruction to choosing a normal-bundle parametrization.

matches.text: The extension to “une immersion locale de topos” is qualified by “sauf erreur,” so the general topos construction is not established here. It adds a new neighborhood operation to the site-independent flag axioms of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 118–119, and to the tentative topos interpretation of germ coverings in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–243. One must define the intended class of immersions and the relevant limit of localizations, then prove that composition supplies the indicated morphism of germs; the existence of slice topoi alone does not settle that neighborhood problem (Artin et al., 1972, Exposé IV, §5).

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

matches.text: The identity for the “trace de $\Sigma_1$” asserts that restricting the neighborhood germ of $\Sigma'$ in $\Sigma''$ to $\Sigma_1$ gives the germ of $\Sigma'\cap\Sigma_1$ in $\Sigma_1$, without requiring $\Sigma'\subset\Sigma_1$. This **adds** a closed-admissible-subset base-change statement to the neighborhood-filter definition in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, whose residual germs also show why an arbitrary trace cannot be identified from its center alone. At the ordinary neighborhood-filter level, closedness of $\Sigma_1\subset\Sigma''$ proves the required cofinality: extend an open neighborhood $U_1\subset\Sigma_1$ to an ambient open $W$, then use $W\cup(\Sigma''\setminus\Sigma_1)$ as a neighborhood of $\Sigma'$. This argument does not apply to an arbitrary nonclosed trace such as a punctured complement, and an analytic-topos version must retain the intended closed-immersion interpretation.

matches.text: The deletion of “séparé” in favour of “un faisceau,” together with the margin read uncertainly as “est connue quand on la connaît localement,” suggests that uniqueness from local data is being distinguished from existence of a global representative. This **adds** a descent question to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where an ambient global divisor already supplies the representative, and **differs** from the categorical recollement of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, which does not settle separatedness of this presheaf of partitions. The relevant question is whether connectedness forces two global partitions with the same local component data to coincide even when compatible local partitions fail to form one admissible global partition. The decisive marginal wording remains uncertain, so this is a proposed interpretation of the revision, not a corrected reading.

matches.text: The claim “contre exemple encore plus simple: les feuilletages!” needs its scope specified, since ordinary foliations of positive transverse dimension have infinitely many local plaques and are not locally finite partitions as in 181 a). The search for local equivalence relations and foliations in the supplied primary files found no matching earlier construction; the nearest germ construction, `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, instead uses a finite local branch set, so the present passage **adds** a broader analogy whose hypotheses are not supplied there. Does “feuilletages” refer to the general SGA theory of local equivalence relations invoked immediately afterwards, or to an intended wider notion of stratification? This question preserves the literal wording and does not import arbitrary foliations into the defined presheaf.

matches.text: Use the drawing with “$7$” incident strata as a concrete test of the germ nerve: the planar model has a central minimum, three ray strata, and three sectors, giving seven objects, nineteen weakly ordered pairs, and thirty-seven weakly ordered triples at the centre. This **adds** a non-Boolean test to the finite powerset models in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106, 116, and 128, while preserving an explicit check of the composable-pair description on scan 188. In the corresponding finite global-chart model, the source spaces are copies of each source closure indexed by its incident chains, so finite étaleness of those projections can hold even though the poset is not Boolean; the example thus separates two properties mentioned together on scan 189. Confidence is high in the finite count and medium in transferring that global-chart topology to every local representative, and no conclusion about reconstruction of an arbitrary stratified space is drawn.

188-03 — The three-ray local poset as a finite calculation

matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

matches.text: The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. Recovering a rational section from an arbitrary compatible family of abstract group splittings is a stronger existence problem and does not follow from closed-point density.

matches.text: The proposed generalization beyond “codim $1$” has a precise formulation for a normal local domain $A$: with compatible choices, $D=G_{\operatorname{Frac}(A^h)}$, $I=G_{\operatorname{Frac}(A^{sh})}$, and $D/I\simeq G_{\kappa(s)}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD, Lemma 58.13.1). This adds a higher-dimensional local statement to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, where the kernel is identified “par Kummer” for a punctured trait. The exact sequence survives this generalization, but the assertion $I\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)$ belongs to the tame one-dimensional situation and must not be transferred to an arbitrary higher-dimensional local ring. Normality and the choices of a geometric point and compatible henselizations should therefore remain visible in any reformulation.

In residue characteristic zero, Hensel’s lemma gives unique $n$th roots in $1+\mathfrak m$, so the compatible Kummer covers for two equal first-order classes identify, as in the later tangent-base-point comparison (Deligne, 1989, §§15.23–15.25). `LM_140-3_text.tex`, scan 238, adds a sharper unresolved question within the supplied manuscript: whether a canonical normalizer section is associated with “l’uniformisante $z$, ou $-z$”, ending “Il faudrait y revenir !”. That contextual sign question does not alter the frozen insertion’s uncertain verb or conormal dual mark, and the Kummer class of a sign must be compared at the specified coefficient level rather than discarded.

matches.text: The reformulation in terms of “éléments de courbe” restates the local reduction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 75, and adds the relative formal completion with its distinguished section. For a smooth curve, the punctured completion and its nonzero tangent line carry the covering-theoretic data used to define a tangential base point (Deligne, 1989, §§15.22–15.26). The statement should therefore be understood as a localization of the cusp-splitting problem, not as saying that the full global fundamental group is determined by one formal disk. The arithmetic descent data and the morphism from that local group into the global group still have to be retained.

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The passage from full “$\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}=H_1$” in c) to one $\ell$-adic component in d) should keep the coefficient convention and residue characteristic explicit. `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 116, restates the boundary contribution to abelianization, while scan 84 adds its cyclotomic Galois action. Our mixed-characteristic check is the good pair $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q_p}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, whose $p$-adic homology $\mathbf Z_p(1)^2$ is ramified although its prime-to-$p$ homology is unramified, so an all-primes reading of c) cannot be equated with d) in the later $p$-adic parenthesis (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Confidence is high because the two Kummer generators give these cyclotomic modules directly; in the original residue-characteristic-zero setting, RN100-03 and RN103-01 separately disprove d)$\Rightarrow$a).

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

matches.text: For “Ladite extension est admissible” on scan 102, the counterexample to e)$\Rightarrow$a) survives the stronger quantifier “for every splitting”: for any section $s:G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the restricted descent cocycle is the continuous quadratic character $\chi_t\circ s$. Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. Confidence is high because the argument restricts the actual geometric descent cocycle before applying fundamental groups, rather than inferring full geometricity from $H_1$.

matches.text: At scan 105, manuscript page 52, (2) defines the precise group by $\pi_1(X;\widetilde X)=\operatorname{Aut}_X(\widetilde X)$. This **restates** the representing-cover viewpoint in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 8–10**, where the covariant fibre functor is $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(S,T)$, but those passages do not explicitly settle the left/right convention in the present formula. Precomposition on $F(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(\widetilde X,W)$ reverses composition, so it identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_X(\widetilde X)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$; using the inverse deck transformation instead gives a left action, exactly the convention issue made explicit in the proof of Lemma 58.3.9 (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BMQ). Confidence: high in the composition calculation and medium in the manuscript's intended convention; the equality need not be called erroneous, but this choice should be fixed before comparing later conjugation and cyclotomic-action formulas.

matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

matches.text: At scan 116, the opening continuation describes finite étale $L$-schemes “non ramifiés sur tout modèle … régulier (propre ou non) de $L/K$”. This **adds** a universal quantifier over models to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, which fixes the henselian local ring of a particular curve at a particular boundary point. With a proper regular model available, the preceding valuative-and-purity argument makes this the category of covers extending étale over that model, and the quotient still includes any arithmetic contribution rather than being the geometric kernel $\pi_{L/K}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB; compare the distinct notation in the present manuscript's (24)–(25)). Confidence: high in that interpretation and in the importance of the universal quantifier.

matches.text: At scan 120, the bracketed “A t-on une réciproque ? regarder !” asks whether triviality of $I_{x'}\to\mathcal E_U^{\overline L}$ implies that the valuation has a center on $U$. This **adds** a converse to the local punctured-trait maps of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Extending the generic-point map to the trait makes every finite étale cover unramified there, proving the forward implication, but factoring the induced group homomorphism does not by itself construct a morphism of schemes, and 120-O1 disproves the unrestricted converse. Confidence: high in this distinction; the separate, faintly stated restriction to elementary $U$ is assessed in 120-CJ1.

matches.text: At scan 121, manuscript page 60, the opening paragraph recovers $\mathcal E_U^{\overline L}$ “en prenant tous les $V$ de $L$ ayant un centre sur $U$” and killing the closed normal subgroup generated by their inertia, adding that codimension-one local rings suffice. This **adds** a quotient presentation to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 26–28**, where the local inertia maps are attached to an already specified curve and boundary. For regular integral finite-type $U/K$, every centered valuation's inertia dies on finite étale covers, while the codimension-one inertia already generates the kernel by finite normalization and regular-target purity (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BTD and 0BMB). Confidence: high with regular $U$; this proves a quotient from the supplied collection of centered valuations, rather than the individual center-detection converse asked on scan 120, and the codimension-one shortcut must not be detached from its regularity hypothesis.

matches.text: The NB beside (31) on scan 121, manuscript page 60, says “Cette définition ne dépend pas de l'hypothèse de résolution des sing” because normal proper models may replace regular ones. This agrees with the modern Riemann–Zariski construction as a locally ringed inverse limit over proper birational models; normal models suffice, and regular models give the same limit when a resolution theorem supplies a cofinal family of them (Temkin, 2011, Introduction and Proposition 2.2.1). It **differs** from **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, whose projective system of group schemes is representable as a scheme because its transition maps are affine, a condition not supplied for the proper birational transitions here. Confidence: high in the resolution-independent normal-model construction and in the conditional cofinality statement; no unrestricted resolution theorem is being assumed.

matches.text: At the end of scan 121, manuscript page 60, “ce n'est pas un schéma !” is qualified by the insertion “si $n\geq2$”, and scan 122 adds that $n=0,1$ are the only scheme cases. For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). Confidence: high under this normal finite-type model interpretation; neither the mere existence of nonnoetherian stalks nor the incorrect noetherian-stalk assertion assessed in 122-CJ1 would prove nonschematicity.

matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

matches.text: At scan 122, the opening continuation of scan 121 says that codimension-one points “correspondent exactement” to the indicated finite-type “jauges”, with “ess.” versus “ext.” still marked as a reading doubt. With the manuscript's codimension $n-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(V)$, lift $n-1$ algebraically independent residue elements to $V$ and choose a normal proper model where those lifts are regular at its center: the center has codimension one, its local ring is a DVR dominated by $V$, and hence equals $V$, giving an essentially finite-type divisorial valuation ring. This **adds** the higher-dimensional residue criterion to the curve-local “anneau-jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, and agrees with the description of Zariski prime divisors by codimension-one local rings and residue transcendence degree in Pop (2006, pp. 294–295). Confidence: high in the divisorial characterization, including the converse supplied by a prime divisor on a normal model; it neither identifies all discrete valuations with divisorial ones nor resolves the abbreviated handwritten adjective.

matches.text: At scan 122, the second paragraph begins “Sauf erreur” and claims that the codimension-zero and codimension-one points are the only ones whose local ring “soit noethérien”. The example and consequence in **130-O1–130-O2** give a valuation ring of $\mathbf Q(x,y)$ with value group $\mathbf Z$ and residue field $\mathbf Q$, hence a noetherian DVR at a point of manuscript codimension two, contradicting this assertion. This **differs** from the divisorial curve-local “jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**: being a DVR is a valuation-theoretic property, whereas being divisorial imposes the additional residue-transcendence condition (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.18, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high because the explicit value group and residue field determine both sides of the contradiction; the counterexample is cross-referenced rather than proved twice.

matches.text: The Proposition in the middle of scan 122 states that “L'application $x\longmapsto\underline O_{\mathfrak X,x}$ est une bijection” onto the valuation rings of $L$ containing $K$, and its proof continues on scan 123. This **adds** a simultaneous description over all models to the single local valuation ring in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**. The classical valuation-space theorem gives this bijection and the stated stalks without requiring regular models: properness supplies compatible centers for a valuation, while blowups provide the local divisibility criterion in the converse direction (Temkin, 2011, Proposition 2.2.1, Lemma 2.2.2, and Corollary 3.4.7). Confidence: high in the normal proper-model formulation; the theorem concerns all valuations containing $K$, including the nondivisorial discrete valuations that invalidate 122-CJ1.

matches.text: The left margin of scan 122 proposes “On pourrait partir de un schéma excellent $X$, et construire un $\mathfrak X$ relatif au dessus”. This **adds** a relative birational space over a general base to the local curve-trait construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**. For an integral base one may use its proper birational modifications and valuations of its function field with centers on it; Temkin's relative construction goes further, using separated morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, without an excellence requirement, and its general stalk description uses semivaluation rings rather than necessarily valuation rings of one field (Temkin, 2011, Sections 1.1 and 2.1–2.2). matches.text: Let $K=\mathbf Q$, choose $h(t)\in\mathbf Q[[t]]$ transcendental over $\mathbf Q(t)$, put $f(t)=t^2+t^3h(t)$, and embed $L=\mathbf Q(x,y)$ into $\mathbf Q((t))$ by $x=t,\ y=f(t)$; such $h$ exists because algebraic elements over the countable field $\mathbf Q(t)$ are countable whereas its coefficient-series set is uncountable. The induced ring $V=L\cap\mathbf Q[[t]]$ has value group $\mathbf Z$, since $v(x)=1$, and residue field $\mathbf Q$, hence is a DVR centered at $(0,0)$ on $X=(\mathbf P^1)^2$ with elementary anabelian open $U=(\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. This adds a nondivisorial DVR test to the jauges of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; see 130-O2 for the noetherian-stalk consequence and 130-O3 for its inertia map. Confidence: high, because injectivity of the field embedding, the value group, and the residue field follow directly from the construction and the DVR criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 00I8).

matches.text: | BISITE D.1 | The actual comparison supplied by open tests. For a space $Y$, put \[ \begin{split} W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Y=\{u:X\longrightarrow X'\text{ over }Y:\quad& \Pi(u^{-1}U):\Pi(X\times_YU)\longrightarrow\Pi(X'\times_YU)\\ &\text{is an equivalence for every open }U\subseteq Y\}. \end{split} \] Here $u^{-1}U$ means the displayed restricted map, not an inverse-image operation on morphisms. This class contains the isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three and retract closure. There is a canonical functor \[ C_Y:(\mathrm{Top}/Y)[(W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Y)^{-1}] \longrightarrow\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal S),\qquad C_Y(X)(U)=\Pi(X\times_YU). \tag{D.1} \] Its values are hypercomplete cosheaves. This statement does not assert that (D.1) is an equivalence for every $Y$. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HA 5.5.5, A.3). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.6 | Proper base change is a coefficient theorem. Consider a cartesian square of locally compact Hausdorff spaces \[ \begin{array}{ccc} X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\[-2pt] {\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\[-2pt] Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y. \end{array} \] If $f$ is proper, the canonical mate $g^*f_*\to f'_*g'^*$ is an equivalence on sheaves of spaces. It is also an equivalence on sheaves with values in a stable bicomplete infinity-category. These are ordinary infinity-sheaves; hypercompletion is not silently substituted. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HTT 7.3.1.18; Volpe). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.7 | A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (Volpe 2025, 3.23–3.27). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.8 | The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. This does not identify $f_!$ with the left adjoint $f_\sharp$ of D.7. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HA 5.5.5.1; Volpe 6.9). |

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: “Si $X$ est compact” is used to obtain finitely many intrinsic strata, “qui sont loc. compactes,” with the warning that finiteness need not survive restriction to an open set. This **adds** a global finiteness conclusion to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where finiteness concerns branch sets at individual points, not the number of global strata. A proof can try a finite cover by charts with finitely many local pieces, but must justify that each local connected piece belongs to one globally constructed stratum; local compactness additionally requires the relevant separation convention and locally closed chart models. These are separate checks, and neither follows simply from finiteness of the local incidence posets.

Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

This adds the family deferred by “Je vais pas le faire ici” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 62, to the cross-ratio description on scan 61. The cross-ratio $t$ meets the boundary, and blowing up the collision of $0$ and $t$ produces two rational components with two marked points and a node on each, so the pointed curve has bad reduction although its compactification is smooth. Confidence is high because the boundary collision and Kummer homology are explicit; only the local $t$-adic inertia is trivial on $H_1$, while the full arithmetic action still contains the cyclotomic character.

This **differs** in scope from **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19 and 25**, where the ambient curve is already projective and smooth. matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

This **adds** a relative birational space over a general base to the local curve-trait construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**. For an integral base one may use its proper birational modifications and valuations of its function field with centers on it; Temkin's relative construction goes further, using separated morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, without an excellence requirement, and its general stalk description uses semivaluation rings rather than necessarily valuation rings of one field (Temkin, 2011, Sections 1.1 and 2.1–2.2). This contradicts the literal negative NB under those model conventions and adds a finite-union test to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; Temkin (2011, Theorem 3.5.1(i)) independently supports the relevant closure property. matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

This restates the peripheral compatibility in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 84, and connects the degeneration to the tangent-parametrized family on scan 79. matches.text: The acknowledgment that “bonne réduction” had been implicit needs the pointed-pair meaning: a proper smooth compactification together with a relatively étale boundary. This restates the finite étale marking condition in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 5, and agrees with Tamagawa’s Definition 5.1 (1997). Smoothness of the compactification alone allows punctures to collide, and even a smooth nonproper model can lose punctures in its special fiber. The genus-zero case proposed in the scan 103 margin therefore tests a real missing boundary condition, as made explicit in RN103-01.

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The margin’s “arithmétisation” should not be treated as a definition of the uncertain adjective following it. In `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 403, an arithmetization is additional structure on a potential curve, accompanied by admissible-lift data, and scan 405 separately asks how to recover that structure. The present margin differs by asserting existence of some arithmetization while the main text asks whether a particular action obtained from a chosen splitting is geometric. Those quantifiers are distinct, so the marginal assertion does not resolve the main admissibility question, whatever the uncertain adjective ultimately means.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: The invitation “Le cas du genre $0$” has an explicit editorial test: $U=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q((t))}\setminus\{0,t,1,\infty\}$ has all four punctures rational and $H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbf Z_\ell)\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell(1)^3$, so its $t$-adic inertia acts trivially for every $\ell$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). This adds the family deferred by “Je vais pas le faire ici” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 62, to the cross-ratio description on scan 61. The cross-ratio $t$ meets the boundary, and blowing up the collision of $0$ and $t$ produces two rational components with two marked points and a node on each, so the pointed curve has bad reduction although its compactification is smooth. Confidence is high because the boundary collision and Kummer homology are explicit; only the local $t$-adic inertia is trivial on $H_1$, while the full arithmetic action still contains the cyclotomic character.

matches.text: The question “comment voir que e) implique bonne réduction” has a counterexample in its stated generality: over $K=\mathbf Q((t))$, let $E_t:y^2=x^3-t^2x$ and $U_t=E_t\setminus\{O\}$, the ramified quadratic twist of $U_0$ for $E_0:y^2=x^3-x$. The isomorphism $(X,Y)\mapsto(tX,t^{3/2}Y)$ over $K(\sqrt t)$ has descent cocycle $[-1]$, so inertia acts as $-1$ on $H_1$ and rules out good reduction, whereas the uniformizer-based residue splitting fixing $\sqrt t$ pulls the full outer action back to that of $U_0/\mathbf Q$ (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). The current passage adds a reduction implication to the realization meaning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410; this example disproves that addition using the local splitting construction of scan 75. Confidence is high because the coordinate change and descent cocycle are explicit; this is an editorial counterexample with finite nontrivial inertia, and no extra semistability assumption is being inserted into the manuscript.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

matches.text: The margin’s “n'est pas étale” concerns integral separation of boundary points, a property stronger than their rationality over the generic field. This differs from `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 150, where the generalized-Jacobian description begins with a boundary already “étale de degré $3$”. In RN103-01, all punctures are rational and their boundary permutation module is constant, yet their closures collide; the abelianized representation consequently loses the cross-ratio degeneration. The proposed genus-zero investigation therefore isolates precisely why a boundary permutation representation, even together with the compactification’s homology, need not recover good reduction of the pointed curve.

This **adds** a larger separably closed field of a base point to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 22**, which describes a separable residue-field closure, and scan 108 of the present manuscript itself explicitly says “clôtures séparables dans $\Omega$”. Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. Confidence: high in this distinction, medium in the intended terminology, and low in the marked subscript; it does not assert invariance of $\pi_1(X_\Omega)$ under changing the base field of $X$.

This **adds** a scheme over $Y$ to the representing-object formulation in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 8, Proposition 1.5**, and to its pointed-cover formulation in scans 9–10. For finite étale covers, the construction is precise when $Z$ is nonempty and connected with trivial étale fundamental group: send a cover $W\to Y$ to $\pi_0(W\times_Y Z)$, since every such pullback is a finite disjoint union of copies of $Z$, and use Galois-category reconstruction for its automorphism group (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BMQ and 0BQ8). Confidence: high for this finite-étale formulation; extending the same wording to all locally constant objects requires retaining the context's separate hypotheses on the topos.

matches.text: At scan 109, manuscript page 54, “une ‘suite exacte d'homotopie universelle’ … (en dim $1$)” introduces the hypothesis used in (12)–(13). This **adds** a universal relative assertion to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 188**, whose specific curve-moduli fibration explicitly retains a preceding $\pi_2$-term before obtaining a short exact sequence. The standard scheme theorem for a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation with connected reduced geometric fibres gives $\pi_1(X_{\bar y})\to\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y)\to 1$, with no initial $1$, so ordinary exactness, injectivity from the fibre, and invariance under the proposed changes of $T$ must be distinguished (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Proposition 58.15.2, Tag 0C0J). Confidence: high that the manuscript needs a stronger or more explicit hypothesis for its fibre-group isomorphisms; no claim is made that the author intended only the weaker standard theorem.

The arithmetic statement is valid for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated $X/K$ with connected geometric fibre: $1\to\pi_1(X_{\bar K})\to\pi_1(X)\to G_K\to 1$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.14.3, Tag 0BTX). It does not justify the stronger assertion for every simply connected $T$, and unrestricted field extension of a nonproper scheme in characteristic $p$ already supplies a counterexample, detailed in 110-O1 (Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). Confidence: high in the arithmetic theorem and in the distinction between it and the unrestricted reading of (12).

This **adds** a relative component factor to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 83**, where a finite base extension separates geometric connected components and makes the relevant images over the base Galois group explicit. A precise finite case is the Stein factorization of a proper flat finitely presented map with geometrically reduced fibres, for which $Y'\to Y$ is finite étale (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.15.1, Tag 0BUN); the closed image of $\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y)$ instead determines a pointed profinite cover in Galois theory, without automatically being an open subgroup or a finite cover. matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

With a proper regular model available, the preceding valuative-and-purity argument makes this the category of covers extending étale over that model, and the quotient still includes any arithmetic contribution rather than being the geometric kernel $\pi_{L/K}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB; compare the distinct notation in the present manuscript's (24)–(25)). matches.text: At scan 116, immediately before (21), “Si $U$ est un modèle quelconque; il se plonge dans un $X$” inherits the proper regular $X$ of scan 115. This **differs** in scope from **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19 and 25**, where the ambient curve is already projective and smooth. Nagata compactification supplies a proper compactification for a separated finite-type $U/K$, but gives no regularity conclusion; a singular $U$ cannot be an open subscheme of a regular $X$, and even for regular $U$ a regular compactification is an additional existence input (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Theorem 38.33.8, Tag 0F41). Confidence: high in the missing qualification; the ensuing quotient calculation is sound for an actual dense open $U\subset X$ with $X$ regular, and must not be used as an argument for unrestricted resolution of singularities.
