matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

The assertion adds a geometric mechanism to the expressly “non-formel” missing first-face map in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 133–135, where only the maps preserving the first flag element had been constructed. A proof must produce the functor on covering categories, show that it is independent of the tubular choices, and verify its compatibility with the already defined face and degeneracy maps; the curve construction of Deligne (1989, §§15.3–15.7) provides a precise comparison case, not a proof of the full flag statement.

It restates the obstruction already explicit in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 135, “mais non un morphisme entre les espaces avec $*$,” while adding a proposed solution through neighborhood germs. This also connects to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 262, which identifies the absence of a direct map between the punctured germ and the tangent-direction circle as the difficulty solved by its invariant functor; comparing these two constructions is more precise than treating generization as an ordinary map of bundles.

matches.text: Defining the fundamental groupoids “par revêtements et isomorphismes entre tels” requires a decision about which coverings are retained. The passage restates the covering-category approach of `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 246–249, and the multigaloisian reconstruction of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 7–8; those passages discuss universal coverings and ordinary groups, whereas SGA 1's Galois categories use finite coverings and profinite groups (Grothendieck & Raynaud, 2003, Exposé V, §5). A comparison must therefore state whether it concerns all topological coverings, finite coverings, or a completion, and must not silently replace the manuscript's discrete lattice kernels by profinite lattices.

matches.text: The combination of “topos quasi-galoisien” with a topological category of strata suggests comparing the proposed reconstruction with a stratified shape rather than immediately taking an ordinary groupoid. This **adds** a potential bridge to the noninvertible specialization data of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and the site-independent flag axioms in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118: Barwick et al. (2020, §§0.4.7 and 0.5.2, in the author PDF checked here) classify suitable constructible sheaves of $\pi$-finite spaces using profinite stratified shapes, with a Galois-category description for quasicompact quasiseparated schemes. Confidence is medium in this as a useful comparison problem because both constructions retain specialization, but the manuscript's analytic germ flags are not thereby identified with the profinite category of geometric points and étale specializations. Establishing a comparison would require an actual functor, precise coefficients and continuity, and the relevant stratified-topos hypotheses; neither the general analytic case nor full homotopy recovery follows automatically from that theorem.

matches.text: The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. Recovering a rational section from an arbitrary compatible family of abstract group splittings is a stronger existence problem and does not follow from closed-point density.

For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. Confidence is high because the argument restricts the actual geometric descent cocycle before applying fundamental groups, rather than inferring full geometricity from $H_1$.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

The induced ring $V=L\cap\mathbf Q[[t]]$ has value group $\mathbf Z$, since $v(x)=1$, and residue field $\mathbf Q$, hence is a DVR centered at $(0,0)$ on $X=(\mathbf P^1)^2$ with elementary anabelian open $U=(\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. Since $v(x)=1$, $v(y)=2$, and $y/x^2$ has residue 1 and therefore all compatible roots in the henselization, the inertia map has weights $(1,2)$, whose image has infinite index in the rank-two target. This adds a concrete contradiction to the unrestricted open-image assertion beyond the single-uniformizer model of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77, inside the elementary product-hyperbolic scope; the full $N_V\to N_x$ image is also non-open because its intersection with $I_x$ is exactly this inertia image when both residue fields are $\mathbf Q$. matches.text: The claim that $\hat X\setminus D$ « a un caractère invariant » should be tested by comparing the pairs or boundary maps associated with different compactifications, keeping the boundary object separate from the homotopy type of the whole complement. **Context comparison — differs in scope:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 127–133, builds a system on open strata and their normal torsors, not merely a single invariant of the open variety; cote 149’s formulation should retain that additional relative information. Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

matches.text: | BISITE D.13 | A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define the contravariant fully faithful functor \[ \Phi_P(F)=\mathbb V_{\|NP\|}\,E_P^{\max}(DF), \qquad F\in\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{perf}}). \tag{D.13a} \] If $f:P\to Q$ is categorically smooth, then its realization $g$ satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(f_!F)\simeq g_+\Phi_P(F). \tag{D.13b} \] Thus ordinary cosheaf pushforward realizes this specified dual of left Kan extension. The cosheaf subcategories in (D.13a) are defined as Verdier images of maximum-constructible perfect sheaves; they are not being identified with literal minimum-constructible cosheaves. matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: The conclusion “de deuxième espèce” should be compared with the later restriction to splittings arising from a uniformizer, rather than silently identifying those two families. This differs in scope from `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 79, which explicitly distinguishes the whole Kummer-cohomology torsor from a smaller “sous-famille” called geometric and parametrized by a $k^\times$-torsor. Our elementary test over $\mathbf Q$ is a compatible family of classes of $p^{a_n}$, with $(a_n)\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ not arising from an ordinary integer: its valuation at $p$ prevents it from being the Kummer class of any rational number (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Confidence is high because rational valuations are integers, so this supplies explicit non-tangent classes in the local splitting torsor while making no claim to prove a global section conjecture.

Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. Recovering a rational section from an arbitrary compatible family of abstract group splittings is a stronger existence problem and does not follow from closed-point density.

matches.text: The proposed study of what “se passe en les autres points” adds a specialization problem to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 78, which already defers the functorial behavior of the distinguished tangent torsor. An editorial local test is to replace a nonzero conormal section $v$ by $h v$: on the common invertible locus, the change of splitting is the Kummer class of $h$. At a codimension-one zero or pole, its residue is the integer $v(h)$, so the failed nonvanishing condition leaves a calculable ramification contribution rather than a well-defined nonzero tangent vector (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Confidence is high for this local statement because it is the same Kummer valuation computation as RN094-01; a global extension across singular strata is not asserted.

The statement should therefore be understood as a localization of the cusp-splitting problem, not as saying that the full global fundamental group is determined by one formal disk. matches.text: The desired “vue d’ensemble” can be organized by composing group homomorphisms over the arithmetic quotient, with residue-field maps supplied by decomposition groups rather than by nonexistent canonical inclusions $k(s)\subset K$. This adds a comparison between the local groupoid in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, and the conjugacy classification of splittings on scan 63 (“mod. autom. intérieurs”). For a fixed based extension, a splitting gives an actual conjugation action on its geometric kernel, whereas changing the base point or transport path changes the comparison by an inner automorphism. The latter dependence is explicit in SGA 1, Exposé XIII, §2.10, and explains why the author’s insistence on “effectives” requires compatible choices (Grothendieck, 1971/2003).

This restates the warning in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, that the residue algebraic closure is not canonically the previously chosen closure of the ground field. Taking the complete regular curve model organizes its places intrinsically, but does not remove the conjugacy choice of a lift $s^{\prime}$ or supply a preferred splitting of $D_{s^{\prime}}\to G_{k(s)}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). Tamagawa proves that good reduction of the pair is equivalent to trivial outer inertia on one, equivalently every, prime-to-residue-characteristic pro-$\ell$ geometric fundamental group (Tamagawa, 1997, Theorem 5.3). This adds a group criterion to the marked-curve setting of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 5, with its “fini étale” boundary. matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. (2015, Theorem 1.1), with Serre and Tate (1968) retained as the original bibliographic reference. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The answer “Sans doute pas” to “est-elle admissible ?” is supported here only by asking which curve could realize the action if the expected smooth reduction does not exist. This restates the realization meaning of “action ext. admissible” in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, but does not force a realizing curve to be the literal special fiber of the given model. The ramified quadratic-twist calculation in RN103-03–RN103-04 supplies a different realizing curve over the residue field and therefore refutes that inference in the stated generality. matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

This restates the open-subgroup issue in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 412, whose reverse direction is explicitly queried by “et inversement ?”. Such a restriction should not be identified with a ramified extension of the local generic field that kills its inertia: decomposition and residue quotients distinguish those operations (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). For instance, the twist in RN103-03 becomes constant after adjoining $\sqrt t$, whereas its residual action is already geometric over $\mathbf Q$ before making any residue extension.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

matches.text: For “Ladite extension est admissible” on scan 102, the counterexample to e)$\Rightarrow$a) survives the stronger quantifier “for every splitting”: for any section $s:G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the restricted descent cocycle is the continuous quadratic character $\chi_t\circ s$. Kummer theory realizes it by a quadratic twist $U_0^{(d)}/\mathbf Q$, so the full pulled-back outer action, and hence its center-free-kernel extension, is geometric; the fixed point $(0,0)$ also supplies the corresponding geometric actual lift (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK; Tamagawa, 1997, Lemma 7.1). This contradicts the proposed implication even with the splitting quantifier strengthened, while restating the “réalisable” interpretation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 410, and adding an explicit calculation to the splitting classes on scan 63. Confidence is high because the argument restricts the actual geometric descent cocycle before applying fundamental groups, rather than inferring full geometricity from $H_1$.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

This differs from `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 150, where the generalized-Jacobian description begins with a boundary already “étale de degré $3$”. In RN103-01, all punctures are rational and their boundary permutation module is constant, yet their closures collide; the abelianized representation consequently loses the cross-ratio degeneration. The proposed genus-zero investigation therefore isolates precisely why a boundary permutation representation, even together with the compactification’s homology, need not recover good reduction of the pointed curve.

Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. The Artin–Schreier cover $z^p-z=tx$ of $X_T$ gives a class in $\Omega[x]/\{h^p-h\}$ outside the image of $k[x]/\{h^p-h\}$, so the natural $\pi_1(X_T)\to\pi_1(X)$ cannot be an isomorphism although $T$ is $1$-connected (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0A3J; compare the same obstruction in Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). This **differs** from the characteristic-zero curve setting of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19–22**, and does not affect scan 106's change of the field of a base point while keeping $X$ fixed. Confidence: high, because polynomial Artin–Schreier classes detect the failure explicitly; this is an application of a known obstruction to the manuscript's wording, not a claim of a new counterexample in the literature.

matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

Both maps to the inertia of the crossing $(0,0)$ have Kummer weights $(1,2)$, hence give the same image conjugacy class in the fixed product $U=(\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, as computed in 130-O3. This adds a failure of injectivity for valuation images on one model to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 117–118, and differs from separating distinct curve cusps because both valuations have the same boundary center. Confidence: high for this fixed-model statement, because both the distinguishing function and the inertia weights are explicit; equality of inertia subgroups in $G_L$ or of their images on all models is not asserted.

matches.text: Let $K=\mathbf Q$, choose $h(t)\in\mathbf Q[[t]]$ transcendental over $\mathbf Q(t)$, put $f(t)=t^2+t^3h(t)$, and embed $L=\mathbf Q(x,y)$ into $\mathbf Q((t))$ by $x=t,\ y=f(t)$; such $h$ exists because algebraic elements over the countable field $\mathbf Q(t)$ are countable whereas its coefficient-series set is uncountable. The induced ring $V=L\cap\mathbf Q[[t]]$ has value group $\mathbf Z$, since $v(x)=1$, and residue field $\mathbf Q$, hence is a DVR centered at $(0,0)$ on $X=(\mathbf P^1)^2$ with elementary anabelian open $U=(\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. This adds a nondivisorial DVR test to the jauges of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77; see 130-O2 for the noetherian-stalk consequence and 130-O3 for its inertia map. Confidence: high, because injectivity of the field embedding, the value group, and the residue field follow directly from the construction and the DVR criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 00I8).

matches.text: The valuation in 130-O1 has manuscript codimension $2-\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf Q=2$, but its stalk is the noetherian DVR $V$; every nonzero ideal is generated by an element of least nonnegative valuation. This contradicts the tentative assertion on 122, main rows 3–6, that only the codimension-zero and codimension-one points have noetherian stalks, under the all-valuations interpretation subsequently proved on 122–123 (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 00I8, Lemma 10.50.18). It adds a distinction between a DVR and a divisorial, essentially finite-type DVR to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77, where no all-valuations codimension classification is given. Confidence: high for this precise counterexample, because its codimension and noetherianity are independent direct computations; it does not contradict the correct codimension-one classification restricted to the essentially finite-type jauges.

matches.text: For 130-O1, the characteristic-zero DVR calculation gives $I_V\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)$, whereas the two-branch local Kummer calculation gives $I_x\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)^2$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BUA; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XIII, Corollary 5.6). Since $v(x)=1$, $v(y)=2$, and $y/x^2$ has residue 1 and therefore all compatible roots in the henselization, the inertia map has weights $(1,2)$, whose image has infinite index in the rank-two target. This adds a concrete contradiction to the unrestricted open-image assertion beyond the single-uniformizer model of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 75–77, inside the elementary product-hyperbolic scope; the full $N_V\to N_x$ image is also non-open because its intersection with $I_x$ is exactly this inertia image when both residue fields are $\mathbf Q$. Confidence: high, because the Kummer characters explicitly compute the map; the target is the abstract local inertia, not an assumed global embedding, and the example does not refute the master section conjecture.

Pulling back to $S^2$ reduces this to the degrees of the clutching maps, with first Chern class equal to the oriented Euler obstruction (Hatcher, 2017, Example 1.10 and Propositions 1.11,3.13(c),3.22). This adds a computable description of the missing map using exactly the normal-bundle data already present in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, and refines its sufficient $\pi_2=0$ condition in scan 130 to vanishing of those evaluations. Confidence: high in that locally trivial complex model, because pullback and clutching compute the boundary map directly; an étale or formal analogue requires its own comparison and is not asserted here.

matches.text: The phrase « l'action extérieure “cyclotomique” » invites a comparison between the system of maps $T^J\to\pi_{U/K}$ and the stabilizers of all roots of the boundary divisors: in characteristic zero, their geometric fibers involve $\varprojlim_n\mu_n^J$, with the arithmetic cyclotomic action and, when branches are not globally labeled, their permutation action. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, describes the corresponding integral local systems and torus torsors, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, identifies the one-branch inertia with a Tate module in its discussion of tangential splittings. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3 and Theorem 6.22) identify the relevant Kummer étale topos with that of the infinite root stack, providing a candidate precise setting for this comparison. **Our confidence: medium**, since the local stabilizers and actions agree in the characteristic-zero normal-crossing case, but this alone neither proves that their maps into a global fundamental group are injective nor recognizes all valuations from that group.

matches.text: The claim that $\hat X\setminus D$ « a un caractère invariant » should be tested by comparing the pairs or boundary maps associated with different compactifications, keeping the boundary object separate from the homotopy type of the whole complement. **Context comparison — differs in scope:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 127–133, builds a system on open strata and their normal torsors, not merely a single invariant of the open variety; cote 149’s formulation should retain that additional relative information. Carchedi et al. (2025; §5 of the linked 2019 preprint) identify the profinite logarithmic homotopy type with the complement’s profinite étale homotopy type for fine saturated, log regular, locally Noetherian schemes over a characteristic-zero field, but that statement by itself does not identify a punctured formal neighborhood with the whole complement. **Our confidence: high** in this distinction, because for a punctured smooth complex curve the boundary is a disjoint union of circles while the open curve usually has a connected and different homotopy type; the precise compactification-independent boundary construction remains the proposed task.

matches.text: The reference to $\mathfrak m_{s_\alpha}/\mathfrak m_{s_\alpha}^{2}$ and the « faisceau conormal » suggests tracing a chosen first-order parameter through the normal-torus construction used for higher-codimension boundary strata. **Context comparison — adds a link:** `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 73–75, treats Kummer torsors of tangential splittings, whereas `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, constructs punctured **normal** line bundles and their product torsors; the conormal line on scan 95 is their dual in the Cartier-divisor situation. A useful check is to compute the effect of $t\mapsto ut$ on the associated splitting class and to track the duality when comparing Chern classes, rather than identifying the two torsor conventions by notation alone (Talpo & Vistoli, 2018, §3, supplies a modern divisor-root framework). **Our confidence: medium**, because the first-order and line-bundle data are visibly present in both manuscripts, but a full identification must specify the parameter, basepoint, and duality conventions.

matches.text: The references below give the editions and primary texts used for the mathematical comparisons. The original Serre–Tate article was bibliographically verified, but its scanned body was not readable through the available reader; the precise criterion invoked here was checked in Andreatta et al. Grothendieck and Murre (1971) is a framework reference checked through the publisher's description and contents, not a source for an asserted theorem about the manuscript's undefined “ombre”; Pop (2010) is used only for the scope stated in its publisher's abstract. Where an author preprint was consulted, a difference from published numbering is stated explicitly.

matches.text: | BISITE D.11 | The realization comparison for every proper map of finite posets. Let $f:P\to Q$ be a $W_\infty$-proper map of finite posets. Equivalently, for every $p\in P$ and $q\geq f(p)$ the outgoing lifting poset \[ L(p,q)=\{r\in P:r\geq p,\ f(r)=q\} \tag{D.11a} \] is weakly contractible. With the minimum stratifications, the topological direct image $\|Nf\|_*$ preserves constructibility and identifies with the categorical $f_*$, including its adjunction data. This holds for spaces, spectra, and the derived category of modules over any ring. Thus the requested geometric class contains the realizations of all such proper functors, with the specified constructibility property, although mere topological properness does not suffice by D.9. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. matches.text: | BISITE D.13 | A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define the contravariant fully faithful functor \[ \Phi_P(F)=\mathbb V_{\|NP\|}\,E_P^{\max}(DF), \qquad F\in\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{perf}}). \tag{D.13a} \] If $f:P\to Q$ is categorically smooth, then its realization $g$ satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(f_!F)\simeq g_+\Phi_P(F). \tag{D.13b} \] Thus ordinary cosheaf pushforward realizes this specified dual of left Kan extension. The cosheaf subcategories in (D.13a) are defined as Verdier images of maximum-constructible perfect sheaves; they are not being identified with literal minimum-constructible cosheaves. For a noncommutative ring the target coefficients are modules over its opposite ring. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. |

The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |

matches.text: The question “Et que se passe-t-il pour $s\notin S^{\prime}$ ?” suggests an editorial calculation at a regular point where the exceptional divisor has simple normal crossings. This adds local section data to the branch bookkeeping in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 107, rather than assuming that a single rank-one inertia group captures every branch. If a boundary parameter pulls back as $u\prod_{j=1}^{r}t_j^{m_j}$, Kummer theory sends the $j$th tame inertia generator to $m_j$ times the target generator, while the unit supplies the residual Kummer class (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Confidence is high for this explicit local calculation, but its globalization needs additional choices; Deligne’s higher-dimensional discussion in §15.2 is itself a proposed framework, whereas his subsequent detailed construction treats curves (Deligne, 1989).

matches.text: The proposed study of what “se passe en les autres points” adds a specialization problem to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 78, which already defers the functorial behavior of the distinguished tangent torsor. An editorial local test is to replace a nonzero conormal section $v$ by $h v$: on the common invertible locus, the change of splitting is the Kummer class of $h$. At a codimension-one zero or pole, its residue is the integer $v(h)$, so the failed nonvanishing condition leaves a calculable ramification contribution rather than a well-defined nonzero tangent vector (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Confidence is high for this local statement because it is the same Kummer valuation computation as RN094-01; a global extension across singular strata is not asserted.

matches.text: The margin “dans le contexte des VA” plausibly alludes to the abelian-variety good-reduction criterion, but neither the abbreviation nor this autobiographical claim identifies a particular publication. Its terminology restates the use of “V.A.” and $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 64, but that passage concerns recognizing points and does not establish a curve-reduction theorem. The Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich–Serre–Tate criterion detects good reduction of an abelian variety from its prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module; the precise statement was checked in Andreatta et al. For a proper curve this controls its Jacobian, and the compact-type example below prevents transferring the criterion to the curve itself.

matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

matches.text: At scan 115, manuscript page 57, the final paragraph says that the quotient of $\mathcal E_L^{\overline L}$ “ne … dépend pas du modèle $X$ choisi”, for $X$ proper and regular. This **adds** a birationally invariant quotient to the local curve-boundary construction in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 25–28**. Given two such models, a finite étale cover of one is unramified at every $K$-valuation by the valuative criterion of properness, hence at the codimension-one local rings of the other, and its finite normalization over the other is étale by regular-target purity; thus the quotient of the fixed $G_L$, not merely its abstract isomorphism type, agrees (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BQJ and 0BMB). Confidence: high when the proper regular models exist; this comparison does not itself prove their existence or require a general resolution theorem to compare two already given models.

This agrees with the modern Riemann–Zariski construction as a locally ringed inverse limit over proper birational models; normal models suffice, and regular models give the same limit when a resolution theorem supplies a cofinal family of them (Temkin, 2011, Introduction and Proposition 2.2.1). For a finitely generated field extension $L/K$, the zero-dimensional space is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and in transcendence degree one the normal proper curve already represents the valuation space; in higher transcendence degree, 121-O1 supplies a separate obstruction to any affine open neighborhood. This **differs** from the affine-transition limit in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**, and is compatible with Olberding's criterion relating affine subspaces of a Zariski–Riemann space to Prüfer intersection rings (Olberding, 2015, Proposition 6.1; preprint Theorem 6.1). matches.text: For “ce n'est pas un schéma !” at the end of scan 121, the following argument **adds** a justification and explains the **difference** from the affine-transition construction in **LM_140-4_text.tex, scans 23–24**. Suppose a nonempty open $W$ of the classical Riemann–Zariski space were affine: its quasi-compactness gives $W=p^{-1}(W_0)$ for an open $W_0$ of a suitable normal proper finite-type model (Temkin, 2011, Lemma 3.4.6), and $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(W_0,\mathcal O)$, since a section is a common rational function and the codimension-one valuation rings on normal $W_0$ force it to be regular there (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.157.6, Tag 031T). Choose a closed regular point $a\in W_0$, blow it up, choose two distinct closed points of the exceptional $\mathbf P^{n-1}_{\kappa(a)}$, and choose valuation rings dominating their local rings: they are distinct points of $W$ with the same center $a$, so both induce the same prime $\mathfrak m_a\cap A$, contradicting $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 10.50.2, Tag 00I8). Confidence: high for $n=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L\geq2$ in this model category, because normality, descent of the quasi-compact open, and distinct centers on the blowup supply the three required steps; this is a proof supplied for the manuscript claim, with no novelty assertion.

With the manuscript's codimension $n-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(V)$, lift $n-1$ algebraically independent residue elements to $V$ and choose a normal proper model where those lifts are regular at its center: the center has codimension one, its local ring is a DVR dominated by $V$, and hence equals $V$, giving an essentially finite-type divisorial valuation ring. This **adds** the higher-dimensional residue criterion to the curve-local “anneau-jauge” in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 25**, and agrees with the description of Zariski prime divisors by codimension-one local rings and residue transcendence degree in Pop (2006, pp. 294–295). The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. This **adds** an explicit example to the normal-line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, and the $\pi_2$ caveat on scan 130, and tests the models on current scans 175–178 as well as the earlier qualification on scan 148. Confidence is high in the calculation because the identification is explicit, and medium in its usefulness for the full diagram comparison because one piece does not settle canonical transition maps; no claim is made that this particular bundle occurs in the moduli application.

The phrase “seul le facteur $I_{s^{\prime}}\simeq T$” isolates the inertia left before a residual section can be chosen. This restates the splitting problem in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73 (“un torseur”), with scan 82 calling the peripheral extension trivial: split does not mean that its cyclotomic conjugation action is trivial. For an equicharacteristic-zero henselian trait, a uniformizer supplies a splitting, and its inertia-conjugacy classes form a torsor under $H^1(k,\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1))\simeq\varprojlim_n k^\times/(k^\times)^n$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). Thus the asserted second-species section is a choice in that torsor, rather than a canonical removal of the Kummer factor.

matches.text: The qualified assertion about “l’ens des pts fermés” is valid as a uniqueness statement for already existing morphisms from a reduced finite-type scheme over a field to a separated target, provided their restrictions as morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Y$ agree, including the residue-field maps. Indeed, the equalizer is closed and contains every closed point, so density and reducedness force equality as morphisms; finite-type schemes over fields are Jacobson (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 01T9). The present passage adds this specialization family to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63 (“classes de scindages”), while scan 64 already marks the unrestricted point–section bijection “faux tel quel”. Recovering a rational section from an arbitrary compatible family of abstract group splittings is a stronger existence problem and does not follow from closed-point density.

This adds a comparison between the local groupoid in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, and the conjugacy classification of splittings on scan 63 (“mod. autom. intérieurs”). matches.text: The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.

The ramified quadratic-twist calculation in RN103-03–RN103-04 supplies a different realizing curve over the residue field and therefore refutes that inference in the stated generality. The Tate-cusp calculation in RN103-05 gives a separate case where geometric realization really is obstructed, so bad reduction alone does not decide this question.

matches.text: The question “qu’attendre d’une telle action ?” can first be separated into its formal and geometric parts. It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. After fixing one section $s$, another has the form $s^{\prime}(g)=c(g)s(g)$ with $c$ a continuous nonabelian $1$-cocycle in $\pi$, and its action is $\operatorname{Int}(c(g))\alpha_s(g)$. Thus changing the section of (31) preserves the outer action but can change the actual action and its point-theoretic interpretation; this is a direct calculation from multiplication in the extension.

This restates the “maquette” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 11, and adds an arithmetic question to the three boundary partitions of the four-pointed line on scan 61. matches.text: The insertion “ou un” is justified, provided a splitting of (31) exists and the assertion means that its $T$-action is inner. The geometric hyperbolic group is center-free, so $\pi\simeq\operatorname{Inn}(\pi)$ identifies an inner-valued action of $T$ with a continuous homomorphism $T\to\pi$ (Tamagawa, 1997, Proposition 1.11). This restates the distinction between splittings and kernel conjugacy in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63: the outer restriction is independent of the selected lift. It does not assert that the resulting homomorphism $T\to\pi$ is zero, and an existential “one splitting” should not be replaced by a vacuous universal statement when no splitting is available.

Our mixed-characteristic check is the good pair $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Q_p}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, whose $p$-adic homology $\mathbf Z_p(1)^2$ is ramified although its prime-to-$p$ homology is unramified, so an all-primes reading of c) cannot be equated with d) in the later $p$-adic parenthesis (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

This restates the open-subgroup issue in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 412, whose reverse direction is explicitly queried by “et inversement ?”. Such a restriction should not be identified with a ramified extension of the local generic field that kills its inertia: decomposition and residue quotients distinguish those operations (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD). For instance, the twist in RN103-03 becomes constant after adjoining $\sqrt t$, whereas its residual action is already geometric over $\mathbf Q$ before making any residue extension.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

This differs from `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 150, where the generalized-Jacobian description begins with a boundary already “étale de degré $3$”. In RN103-01, all punctures are rational and their boundary permutation module is constant, yet their closures collide; the abelianized representation consequently loses the cross-ratio degeneration. The proposed genus-zero investigation therefore isolates precisely why a boundary permutation representation, even together with the compactification’s homology, need not recover good reduction of the pointed curve.

This differs from `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 413, which explicitly anticipates “pathologiques” among lifts of an admissible outer action and treats actual admissibility as an additional condition. The quadratic-twist example supplies geometric outer and actual actions at bad reduction, whereas the Tate example supplies a nongeometric outer action, so neither alone realizes the combination sought here. Constructing that combination would require controlling the section cocycle while retaining a fixed geometric outer action, the separate problem isolated in RN101-03.

This **restates**, in profinite language, the connection between points, fibre functors, and pointed universal covers in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 8–10**, while scan 16 of that file announces a separate pro-multigaloisian variant. A precise finite-étale interpretation uses a pro-object representing the fibre functor, as in the construction from pointed Galois objects in the proof of Lemma 58.3.9 (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BMQ); the context supports this interpretation without deciding whether the literal $\mathcal E_X$ was intended as a classifying-topos abbreviation. matches.text: At scan 106, display (4) and its following sentence, “la clôture alg. de $k(x)$ dans $\Omega$” accompanies a canonical comparison whose first subscript remains $\alpha$ or $X$. This **adds** a larger separably closed field of a base point to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 22**, which describes a separable residue-field closure, and scan 108 of the present manuscript itself explicitly says “clôtures séparables dans $\Omega$”. Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. Confidence: high in this distinction, medium in the intended terminology, and low in the marked subscript; it does not assert invariance of $\pi_1(X_\Omega)$ under changing the base field of $X$.

This **adds** a scheme over $Y$ to the representing-object formulation in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 8, Proposition 1.5**, and to its pointed-cover formulation in scans 9–10. For finite étale covers, the construction is precise when $Z$ is nonempty and connected with trivial étale fundamental group: send a cover $W\to Y$ to $\pi_0(W\times_Y Z)$, since every such pullback is a finite disjoint union of copies of $Z$, and use Galois-category reconstruction for its automorphism group (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BMQ and 0BQ8). Confidence: high for this finite-étale formulation; extending the same wording to all locally constant objects requires retaining the context's separate hypotheses on the topos.

The Artin–Schreier cover $z^p-z=tx$ of $X_T$ gives a class in $\Omega[x]/\{h^p-h\}$ outside the image of $k[x]/\{h^p-h\}$, so the natural $\pi_1(X_T)\to\pi_1(X)$ cannot be an isomorphism although $T$ is $1$-connected (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0A3J; compare the same obstruction in Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). This **differs** from the characteristic-zero curve setting of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19–22**, and does not affect scan 106's change of the field of a base point while keeping $X$ fixed. Confidence: high, because polynomial Artin–Schreier classes detect the failure explicitly; this is an application of a known obstruction to the manuscript's wording, not a claim of a new counterexample in the literature.

This **adds** a relative component factor to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 83**, where a finite base extension separates geometric connected components and makes the relevant images over the base Galois group explicit. A precise finite case is the Stein factorization of a proper flat finitely presented map with geometrically reduced fibres, for which $Y'\to Y$ is finite étale (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.15.1, Tag 0BUN); the closed image of $\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y)$ instead determines a pointed profinite cover in Galois theory, without automatically being an open subgroup or a finite cover. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. matches.text: A useful test of “un quotient de $T$” and “par l’image des $\pi_2$” is the zero-section divisor in the total space of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$: its punctured normal bundle identifies with $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$ by sending a nonzero vector in its tautological line to that vector. This total space retracts to $S^3$, so its fundamental group is zero, whereas the trivial punctured line bundle over $\mathbb P^1$ has fundamental group $\mathbb Z$; the contrast is the Hopf-bundle instance of the connecting map discussed by Serre (1949–1950, §§1, 5). This **adds** an explicit example to the normal-line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–123, and the $\pi_2$ caveat on scan 130, and tests the models on current scans 175–178 as well as the earlier qualification on scan 148. Confidence is high in the calculation because the identification is explicit, and medium in its usefulness for the full diagram comparison because one piece does not settle canonical transition maps; no claim is made that this particular bundle occurs in the moduli application.

This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). matches.text: The question “qu’attendre d’une telle action ?” can first be separated into its formal and geometric parts. It restates the splitting framework of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 63, while scan 413 adds an independent admissibility condition for actual lifts. After fixing one section $s$, another has the form $s^{\prime}(g)=c(g)s(g)$ with $c$ a continuous nonabelian $1$-cocycle in $\pi$, and its action is $\operatorname{Int}(c(g))\alpha_s(g)$. Thus changing the section of (31) preserves the outer action but can change the actual action and its point-theoretic interpretation; this is a direct calculation from multiplication in the extension.

matches.text: The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.

matches.text: For the proposed “Le cas du genre $0$” and the boundary test of RN103-01, an editorial computation makes the lost information explicit: on $F_3=\langle a,b,c\rangle$, the loop around $t=0$ acts, up to orientation, by $\alpha(a)=(ab)a(ab)^{-1}$, $\alpha(b)=(ab)b(ab)^{-1}$, and $\alpha(c)=c$, the square of an elementary braid (Artin, 1947, formulas 14–15). This adds a monodromy calculation to the free-group presentation in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 115, and chooses one of the “trois partitions” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 61. Its abelianization is the identity, but in the class-two quotient an inner action agreeing on $a,b$ would have conjugating abelianization $a+b$ and hence would move $c$ by $[a,c]+[b,c]\ne0$, proving that the outer action is nontrivial. Confidence is high because the non-inner calculation survives in the free pro-$\ell$ class-two quotient, and the comparison of algebraic and topological coverings identifies this braid with geometric étale monodromy (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1).

This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). matches.text: For the first equality introduced by “Je présume” at the bottom of scan 119, the following derivation **adds** a proof to the analogous tentative normalizer assertion in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 84**. Let $F=(L^{\mathrm{sep}})^I=\operatorname{Frac}(V^{\mathrm{sh}})$; it is henselian with value group still $\mathbf Z$, and adjoining an $m$-th root of a uniformizer, for $m>1$ prime to the residue characteristic, shows that $F$ is not separably closed (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BSW and 0ASF). An element normalizing $I$ preserves $F$ and must preserve its rank-one henselian valuation by the F. K. Schmidt–Engler theorem (Geyer & Jarden, 1991, Proposition 1.3), and then preserves its unique extension to $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$, hence lies in $D$; conversely $D$ normalizes $I$, giving $\operatorname{Norm}_{G_L}(I)=D$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Remark 15.113.6, Tag 0EXQ). Confidence: high, because the fixed-field identification, preservation of the discrete value group, and uniqueness of prolongation apply to this same DVR; the argument does not assert a corresponding equality for arbitrary higher-rank valuations.

matches.text: The phrase « l'action extérieure “cyclotomique” » invites a comparison between the system of maps $T^J\to\pi_{U/K}$ and the stabilizers of all roots of the boundary divisors: in characteristic zero, their geometric fibers involve $\varprojlim_n\mu_n^J$, with the arithmetic cyclotomic action and, when branches are not globally labeled, their permutation action. **Context comparison — adds:** `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, describes the corresponding integral local systems and torus torsors, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 73, identifies the one-branch inertia with a Tate module in its discussion of tangential splittings. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3 and Theorem 6.22) identify the relevant Kummer étale topos with that of the infinite root stack, providing a candidate precise setting for this comparison. **Our confidence: medium**, since the local stabilizers and actions agree in the characteristic-zero normal-crossing case, but this alone neither proves that their maps into a global fundamental group are injective nor recognizes all valuations from that group.

matches.text: | BISITE D.8 | The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. This does not identify $f_!$ with the left adjoint $f_\sharp$ of D.7. | claim (return: Known) | Unverified citation (HA 5.5.5.1; Volpe 6.9). |

matches.text: | BISITE D.13 | A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define the contravariant fully faithful functor \[ \Phi_P(F)=\mathbb V_{\|NP\|}\,E_P^{\max}(DF), \qquad F\in\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{perf}}). \tag{D.13a} \] If $f:P\to Q$ is categorically smooth, then its realization $g$ satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(f_!F)\simeq g_+\Phi_P(F). \tag{D.13b} \] Thus ordinary cosheaf pushforward realizes this specified dual of left Kan extension. The cosheaf subcategories in (D.13a) are defined as Verdier images of maximum-constructible perfect sheaves; they are not being identified with literal minimum-constructible cosheaves. For a noncommutative ring the target coefficients are modules over its opposite ring. | claim (return: Proved) | Unverified. |

matches.text: | RESIDUE H.7 | The program \path{code/GHIJ/finite_poset_direct_image.py} independently enumerates all maps between one representative of every poset isomorphism class with at most five objects, including the empty poset. The counts of posets of sizes $0,1,2,3,4,5$ are $1,1,2,5,16,63$. It examines $1,349,916$ monotone maps and recognizes $96,372$ proper maps. Properness is certified by explicit simplicial collapses of every nonempty outgoing lifting order complex; noncontractible cases are rejected by homology over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_2$. The program aborts rather than classifying an acyclic but uncertified complex as contractible. No such undecided case occurs in this range. For every proper map and every nonempty target simplex, it computes the categorical stalk and the actual geometric-fibre cellular cohomology, for the constant coefficient and for each principal-cosieve indicator. This gives $5,536,094$ stalk/coefficient cases, each computed over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_2$, with no discrepancy. A fibre cell is indexed by a source chain meeting each level of the target simplex; it is a product of simplices, of dimension $\|\kappa\|-\|\sigma\|$. Its signed boundary deletes one vertex while keeping every level nonempty, using the product-boundary sign. The code verifies that consecutive boundary matrices multiply to zero. Exact rational ranks use integer elimination with gcd reduction, and binary ranks use bit arithmetic. For a principal cosieve, extension from the corresponding closed subcomplex reduces both computations to its intersection with the relevant fibre or lower inverse image. The supplied per-map CSV records all tests as successful; the JSON gives the totals by source and target size. These numerical comparisons check cohomology, not a replacement proof of the canonical mate; the latter is established in H.1. | claim (return: Proved) | no review |
