matches.text: The phrase “de noyau un quotient de $T_{d_0,\ldots,d_r}$” is consistent with the exact sequence $\pi_2(B)\to\pi_1((\mathbb C^*)^r)\to\pi_1(P)\to\pi_1(B)\to1$ for a locally trivial torus bundle over a connected base. It qualifies the extension description in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 130–131, where the margin already warns that the full lattice kernel requires a condition on $\pi_2$. The connecting homomorphism can kill meridians, so a proof should identify its image and the induced local-system action rather than assert an injection of the entire lattice; the fibration exact sequence is the relevant classical result (Serre, 1949–1950, §1).

matches.text: The claim that the “donnée … est équivalente” to compatible subsets of $\pi_0(D_d)$ makes the admissible closed $\Sigma$ recoverable from the global component data rather than arbitrary local labels. This **adds** a closed-subset classification to the branch-labeling torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 109 and 117, where permutation monodromy is already built into the flag spaces. To prove both directions one must show that the component selections respect the incidence maps and descend to a locally finite union of branch intersections, and that every such union yields exactly those selections. Working with $\pi_0(D_d)$ incorporates the global branch identifications; independently labeling local branches without their transport could produce a selection that does not descend.

matches.text: The inserted phrase “fibré conormal” accompanies an exact sequence with the usual direction of a normal-bundle sequence. This **differs** from the explicit “faisceau normal” construction in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 122, while `LM_140-3_text.tex`, scan 293, shows that a check accent can also occur in the geometric-vector-bundle notation $\check V(\mathcal N)$. Under the standard convention for $Z\hookrightarrow Y\hookrightarrow X$, the conormal sequence starts with $\mathcal C_{Y/X}|_Z$, and dualizing a locally split exact sequence gives $0\to N_{Z/Y}\to N_{Z/X}\to N_{Y/X}|_Z\to0$ (Stacks Project Authors, 2026a, §37.63(4); 2026c, Lemma 31.22.6). This is a convention/readability question for the displayed symbols, not authorization to replace “conormal,” reverse arrows, or remove an accent in the transcription.

The proposed generalization beyond “codim $1$” has a precise formulation for a normal local domain $A$: with compatible choices, $D=G_{\operatorname{Frac}(A^h)}$, $I=G_{\operatorname{Frac}(A^{sh})}$, and $D/I\simeq G_{\kappa(s)}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BSD, Lemma 58.13.1). This adds a higher-dimensional local statement to `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, where the kernel is identified “par Kummer” for a punctured trait. The exact sequence survives this generalization, but the assertion $I\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1)$ belongs to the tame one-dimensional situation and must not be transferred to an arbitrary higher-dimensional local ring. Normality and the choices of a geometric point and compatible henselizations should therefore remain visible in any reformulation.

This restates the punctured-trait-to-residue-point passage in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 26, now applied to the homomorphism produced by the rational point. matches.text: The proposed “courbe modulaire pour courbes elliptiques” can be tested at a split Tate cusp using $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$. This adds a local degeneration calculation to the elliptic modular family in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 517. Tate’s torsion sequence $0\to\mu_n\to E_q[n]\to\mathbf Z/n\to 0$ has Kummer class $q$, so the induced inertia on $H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbf Z_\ell)=T_\ell E_q$ is nontrivial unipotent monodromy (Tate, 1995, torsion discussion, manuscript p. 19). This verifies the author’s predicted nontriviality for the stated test case and supplies the more restrictive residual-action obstruction in RN103-05.

matches.text: The tentative “ne soient géométriques” does hold for the editorial test $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$: after any splitting $G_{\mathbf Q}\to G_K$, the Tate-module semisimplification is $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)\oplus\mathbf Q_\ell$, by Tate’s exact torsion sequence (Tate, 1995, manuscript p. 19). This adds a concrete use of the “non-trivialité à la Weil” proposed in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 85. The weight-zero constituent persists after every finite number-field extension, whereas a hypothetical realizing smooth curve has, at a suitable good finite prime, $H^1$ of weights at least one and therefore no weight-zero constituent in its dual $H_1$ (Deligne, 1980, Corollary 3.3.5). Confidence is high because the obstruction uses only the invariant subquotients and their weights; it proves nongeometricity in this Tate case, without reversing the quadratic-twist counterexample or asserting a universal bad-reduction principle.

matches.text: | BISITE D.13 | A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(\|NP\|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$.
